description: INVALID_DATE is null, yet overlaps() calls _startDTG.equals(INVALID_DATE) and _endDTG.equals(INVALID_DATE) before checking for null, so the documented 'we don't have a start time -> return TRUE' branch is unreachable; verified new BaseTimePeriod(null,null).overlaps(a,b) throws NullPointerException. hashCode() calls getStartDTG().getDate() and also NPEs on the INVALID period (verified), so such periods cannot go in hash collections even though equals() handles nulls. contains(null) likewise NPEs.
trigger_input: Layer or narrative entry with unset start/end (period created via new BaseTimePeriod(null,null) then overlaps(...) during time-filtering).
suggested_fix: Test _startDTG == null / _endDTG == null (or use isInvalid()) before dereferencing; make hashCode null-safe with Objects.hash.
llm_value: grep-able

title: rangeFromEdge mixes Euclidean lat/lon degrees with earth-model ranges
description: distancePointLine computes the projection parameter r and the perpendicular |s|*L in raw (long,lat) degree space with no cos(lat) weighting, but falls back to p.rangeFrom(A)/rangeFrom(B) (earth-model great-circle degrees) when r<=0 or r>=1. The two metrics differ by up to 1/cos(lat) in longitude, so rangeFromEdge is discontinuous at the corner boundaries and over-reports distance to E/W edges at high latitude.
trigger_input: WorldArea at 60N, point due east of the right edge by 1 deg lon: rangeFromEdge returns ~1.0 deg (60 nm) while the corner fallback would return ~0.5 deg (30 nm).
suggested_fix: Perform the segment maths in a locally scaled frame (x scaled by cos(midLat)) or express edges via WorldLocation.rangeFrom to a projected foot point.
llm_value: Needs tracing two different distance metrics through the same branch structure; a type checker sees only doubles.

title: Areas spanning the antimeridian normalise to the complementary near-global box
description: normalise() (and extend/contains) simply take min/max of raw longitudes, so an area whose corners are at 179E and 179W becomes 358 deg wide with TL longitude -179 and BR +179 (verified by compiling). getWidth/getCentre then describe the wrong region, contains() answers for the complement, and fit-to-window in FlatProjection.zoom gives up (width>=360 check) or shows the whole world.
trigger_input: Load a .rep track crossing 180 deg longitude; Fit-to-window shows the whole globe and bounding-area filters exclude the track's fixes.
suggested_fix: Represent longitude extent explicitly (west edge + positive width, or normalise relative to a reference meridian) and update contains/extend/getCentre accordingly.
llm_value: Dateline handling is a domain invariant; the code's min/max logic is locally correct arithmetic.

title: getUnitIndexFor silently maps unknown unit labels to METRES
description: getUnitIndexFor returns 0 (METRES) when the label does not exactly match one of {m,yds,km,nm,minutes,degs,kyds,ft} (case sensitive). It is called from the XML handlers WorldDistanceHandler (L55, L92), GridHandler and ASSET XMLVariance, so a hand-edited or foreign .dpf/.xml with Units="NM" or "nmi" is loaded as metres with no error. WorldSpeed.getUnitIndexFor (L144-L154) and WorldAcceleration.getUnitIndexFor have the identical default.
trigger_input: .dpf containing <WorldDistance Units="NM" Value="10"/> for a range ring: loaded as 10 m.
suggested_fix: Return -1 or throw IllegalArgumentException for unknown labels and have handlers report the error; compare case-insensitively with documented aliases.
llm_value: The default value is only wrong in the context of the XML callers, which a grep for the method does not reveal.
related: WorldSpeed L144-L154; WorldAcceleration L122-L132; MWC/Utilities/ReaderWriter/XML/Util/WorldDistanceHandler.java L55 L92

title: Static shared _myWorldVector and mutable static earth model
description: bearingFrom() and rangeFrom(other) pass the static field _myWorldVector as the result buffer to _model.subtract and then read range/bearing from it; concurrent callers on different threads overwrite each other's result, so a range or bearing can be read from another thread's computation. The earth model itself is a mutable static (_model, setModel) that is replaced at runtime by CorePlugin extension loading and by tests, making all distance results depend on global process state.
trigger_input: Two analysis jobs (e.g. SATC solver and a tote update) compute rangeFrom simultaneously; one receives the other's range value.
suggested_fix: Use a fresh WorldVector (or ThreadLocal) in bearingFrom/rangeFrom; consider making the model final after startup or documenting single-threaded use.
llm_value: Data race on a static buffer is only visible when correlating the private static with callers across threads; grep finds statics but not the race.

title: interpolateFix interpolates longitude linearly across the antimeridian
description: interpolateFix computes dLong = next.lon - prev.lon and adds the proportion, so a leg from 179.5E to 179.5W yields an interpolated longitude near 0 (verified midpoint = 0.0) i.e. a point on the other side of the globe. Used by getNearestTo when interpolation is on, by resampling (decimatePointsTrack), infills and worm-in-hole offsets, so resampled tracks crossing the dateline acquire garbage fixes.
trigger_input: Track crossing 180 degrees longitude with 'Interpolate points' on, or 'Resample data at' applied
suggested_fix: Normalise dLong into (-180,180] before scaling and wrap the resulting longitude, mirroring the existing course handling.
llm_value: The course wrap handling right beside it makes the omission for longitude easy to miss; requires domain reasoning.

title: interpolateFix divides by zero time delta when previous and next share a DTG
description: proportion = thisDelta/timeDiffMicros with no guard; when previous and next have the same time (e.g. TrackSegment.decimateRelativeTMA passes first()==last() for a one-fix leg, WormInHoleOffset passes consecutive fixes that collided) the result is NaN/Infinity and a Fix with NaN lat/lon/course is created and inserted, which then poisons offsets (RelativeTMASegment.setOffset) and bounds.
trigger_input: Relative TMA leg containing a single fix, then resample the parent track
suggested_fix: Return a copy of previous when timeDiffMicros==0 (or when dtg equals either end) instead of dividing.
llm_value: Needs call-site analysis to find inputs where the two fixes coincide.

title: isBearingToPort unboxes null Boolean when host has no fix at cut time
description: isBearingToPort() only assigns _cachedPortBearing when getNearestTo returns a fix; otherwise it returns the null Boolean, which auto-unboxes to NullPointerException. It also dereferences _mySensor._myHost without a null check. Callers: paint() for ambiguous cuts and the 'Keep port/starboard bearing' actions (ditchBearing).
trigger_input: Sensor with ambiguous bearings whose cuts extend before the host track's first fix; right-click such a cut and choose 'Keep port bearing'
suggested_fix: Return a primitive with a defined default (or Boolean.FALSE) when no host fix is found and guard the host reference.
llm_value: Auto-unboxing of a cached Boolean is a subtle control-flow issue, not grep-able.

title: Split absolute TMA legs have null start/end; DTG edits throw NPE
description: TrackWrapper.splitTrack constructs the two halves with new AbsoluteTMASegment(theTMA, p1, loc, null, null), leaving _startTime/_endTime null. setDTG_End/setDTG_Start then call createDataFrom(_startTime,_endTime) which dereferences startTime.getDate(), and getDTG_Start()/getDTG_End() show null in Properties. shear() also leaves System.out debug prints.
trigger_input: Split an absolute TMA leg at a fix, select the new leg and edit 'End time' in Properties
suggested_fix: Derive _startTime/_endTime from the supplied fixes in the copy constructor when null; remove the printlns.
llm_value: Requires following the split path in TrackWrapper into the constructor contract.

title: reconstruct feeds SplineInterpolator <3 or non-increasing samples
description: oneUse=min(2,before.size()) and twoUse=min(3,after.size()) can total 2 points (two one-fix legs), and overlapping legs (before.endDTG >= after.startDTG, allowed by RelativeTMASegment.setDTG_End) give non-monotonic times; SplineInterpolator.interpolate then throws NumberIsTooSmallException/NonMonotonicSequenceException from inside a PropertyChangeListener or paint cycle. The two-arg constructor also calls before.last().getColor() on a possibly empty segment.
trigger_input: Generate an infill between two legs, then extend the earlier leg's DTG End past the later leg's start
suggested_fix: Validate n>=3 and strictly increasing times before interpolating; fall back to linear interpolation or clear the infill with a logged error.
llm_value: Needs the commons-math precondition knowledge plus the leg-editing paths that can violate it.

title: getNearestTo returns {null} array; callers dereference [0]
description: When the DTG is outside the track period, getNearestTo returns new Watchable[]{null} instead of EMPTY_WATCHABLE_LIST, so callers that test length>0 (ArrayOffsetHelper.getArrayCentre L174, TrackWrapper-style consumers) dereference null. DynamicTrackShapeSetWrapper.paintOverride already defends against list[0]==null, evidence the bug is being hit. getUnfilteredItems also dereferences getStartDTG() on an empty track.
trigger_input: Lightweight track (e.g. imported from a large REP/NMEA set) with a sensor whose cut time is outside the track period; open the plot
suggested_fix: Return EMPTY_WATCHABLE_LIST when nearest==null.
llm_value: Requires reading the contract of the sibling TrackWrapper implementation and its callers.

title: fanStretch mis-normalises drag angle; drags near north reverse range sign
description: theBrg = 2pi+vector.getBearing() lies in [pi,3pi] and midBrg in [0,2pi); theDelta is only reduced while > 2pi, leaving values in (-pi,2pi]. A delta of e.g. 6.08 rad (true separation 0.2 rad) fails abs(theDelta)>pi/2 in the wrong direction and the range is negated (verified), so dragging the fan outward near the sensor bearing's north crossing moves the solution inward.
trigger_input: Fan-stretch drag of a relative TMA leg whose mid bearing is within a few degrees of north, dragging on the other side of north
suggested_fix: Normalise theDelta into (-pi,pi] (while > pi subtract 2pi, while < -pi add 2pi) before the abs test.
llm_value: Requires range analysis of composed bearing offsets; the loop looks like a normalisation.

title: Unchecked sensor/layers/host lookups in DTG editing, rotate and remove
description: setDTG_Start dereferences getReferenceTrack() (may be null before identify), _referenceSensor.getSensorOffset() (null when the segment references a track without a matching sensor, which setTrack merely logs) and hostFix.getLocation() (getBacktraceTo returns null when no visible fix). rotate() calls hostReference.add() where getHostLocation() can return null; identifyReferenceTrack dereferences _theLayers which is null for segments built via the test/legacy constructor; removeElement calls elements().nextElement() on an already-empty segment.
trigger_input: Relative TMA leg whose named sensor was renamed/deleted, then edit 'DTG Start' in Properties
suggested_fix: Null-check the sensor/track/backtrace results and log+return, matching the pattern already used in getHostLocation().
llm_value: Needs knowledge of which lookups are allowed to fail (setTrack logs and continues).

title: stretch() uses exact WorldLocation.equals to pick dragged end
description: rotate() and shear() (L820-L826, L1210-L1216) explicitly avoid WorldLocation.equals because DR rendering shifts the first fix by tiny amounts, yet stretch() still uses first.getLocation().equals(origin). When equality fails while the user drags the far end, the else branch relocates the start along an essentially zero-length thisLeg with an arbitrary bearing, throwing the leg origin to a random position. AbsoluteTMASegment.rotate/shear/stretch (L258, L333, L418) have the same exact test.
trigger_input: Stretch-drag the end of a relative TMA leg after it has been shifted/dragged once
suggested_fix: Reuse the distFromOrigin<distFromEnd test used by rotate/shear in stretch() and in AbsoluteTMASegment.
llm_value: The inconsistency is only evident by comparing sibling methods and reading the comment that explains why equals is unsafe.

title: Integer time division in DR append; unguarded interval division in resample
description: append() for DR segments computes timeSecs as a long division (millis/1000), so fixes under 1 s apart give spdYps=Infinity and coarser gaps are truncated, corrupting the joining fix's course/speed used by DR reconstruction (mergeAllSegments/combineSections). decimateRelative (L711) and setResampleDataAt (L1089) divide by the interval before the <=0 guard, so a 0 interval throws ArithmeticException.
trigger_input: Merge two DR track segments whose boundary fixes are 0.5 s apart; or choose frequency 'None' on a segment
suggested_fix: Use double seconds and guard zero deltas; hoist the <=0 interval check above the divisions.
llm_value: Integer-vs-double division is invisible to a grep; needs unit reasoning.

title: rangeFrom/paint/getSegmentFor assume a non-empty segment
description: rangeFrom() calls getTrackStart() (getData().iterator().next()) before the isEmpty() check, so an empty segment (an infill shown as '[Recalculating]') throws NoSuchElementException from TrackWrapper.findNearestSegmentHotspotFor during a drag/hit test. paint() ends with drawMyStalk(dest,lastPoint,lastButOne,true) where lastButOne is null for a one-fix segment (NPE) and drawMyStalk divides xDelta/yDelta (Infinity for a horizontal pair). SegmentList.getSegmentFor dereferences endDTG() which is null for an empty segment.
instances: L818; L898; L964; L969-L975; TrackWrapper_Support L326
trigger_input: Track containing an infill that could not be generated (empty), then drag-select near the track
suggested_fix: Check isEmpty() first in rangeFrom, guard the stalk drawing for <2 points, and null-check endDTG in getSegmentFor.
llm_value: Ordering bug between a guard and the call it should protect; needs reading, not grepping.

title: Stale caches: getNearestTo _lastFix/_lastPosIterator and rangeFrom _myWorldArea
description: flushPositionCache() is an empty method, so after addFix/removeElement/setDTG the cached _lastFix and _lastPosIterator remain: getNearestTo(T) returns a deleted fix if T was the last time requested, and the cached iterator's currentElement() may be a removed fix. The cache is also keyed on time alone, so a call with onlyVisible=false caches a hidden fix that a later onlyVisible=true call returns, and the cached-iterator path sets previous=thisPos without checking visibility, so interpolation can use a hidden fix. Similarly _myWorldArea (used by rangeFrom) is only built in addFix and never updated by add(TrackSegment), shift/drag or removeElement, so tracks assembled from segments (TMA tracks, split/merge/paste results) return INVALID_RANGE and moved tracks use stale bounds for hit-testing.
trigger_input: Step the time slider to fix F, delete F from the Outline view, tote/plot still reports F for that time
suggested_fix: Clear _lastFix and _lastPosIterator in flushPositionCache() and call it from every mutation path; include onlyVisible in the cache key; derive rangeFrom from getBounds() or rebuild _myWorldArea lazily.
llm_value: Requires noticing that a method named flush* is a no-op and tracing stale-state consequences across calls.

title: Merge/contiguous/visibility helpers NPE on SegmentList, empty or hidden data
description: checkTheyAreNotOverlapping leaves _periods[i] null for a SegmentList subject (which mergeTracks explicitly supports at L676) or builds a period from null start/end for an empty track, then calls timePeriod.overlaps(...) -> NPE. WrappedIterators() leaves currentIter null, so contiguousElements().hasMoreElements() throws when sensors/solutions are hidden and the Positions layer is hidden (DblClickEdit uses it). visibleBetween dereferences getStartDTG() on an empty track; groupTracks calls ts.startDTG().getDate() on an empty segment.
trigger_input: Select a track's 'Positions' folder plus another track and choose Merge Tracks
suggested_fix: Handle SegmentList in checkTheyAreNotOverlapping and skip null periods; initialise currentIter to EmptyIterator; null-check start/end DTGs.
llm_value: Requires correlating supported subject types in mergeTracks with the helper's instanceof chain.

title: Integer-second time delta gives divide-by-zero rates for sub-second or duplic...
description: timeDeltaSecs is computed with integer division (millis/1000L), so two cuts less than one second apart, or two cuts with the same DTG, give timeDeltaSecs==0. gapRate = |valueDelta/0| becomes Infinity (or NaN when valueDelta==0) and brgRate likewise; Infinity > minZig forces a zig, NaN silently fails every comparison. Neither case is guarded and the caller receives wrong leg boundaries with no error.
trigger_input: .rep with SENSOR2 lines at 500 ms spacing (e.g. 120000.000 and 120000.500) or two cuts with identical DTG on one towed-array sensor.
suggested_fix: Compute the delta in double seconds (millis/1000d) and skip or merge cuts whose time delta is <= 0.
llm_value: Requires noticing the long division and tracing how Infinity/NaN propagate through the threshold logic.

title: resolve() crashes on empty legs and silently skips single legs; chunkFor can ...
description: getPermutations()/midTimeFor() call leg.get(0) and leg.get(size-1) without checking for an empty LegOfCuts, and valueAt() dereferences the null curve that getCurve() returns for an empty leg (IndexOutOfBounds / NPE). With exactly one leg walkScores() produces a single empty ScoreList so the leg is never resolved and an empty list is returned without warning. chunkFor(len,9) returns -1 for len in {723,1009,1028,...} (python enumerated 25 values < 5000) so subList(0,-1) throws.
trigger_input: Resolve Ambiguity with an ownship zone dragged over a period containing no visible TA cuts (BearingResidualsView.resolveAmbiguousCutsB builds an empty LegOfCuts for it), or with a single zone.
suggested_fix: Filter out empty legs (and legs with < 3 cuts) before getPermutations; handle the single-leg case explicitly; make chunkFor fall back to MAX_CHUNK_SIZE instead of -1.
llm_value: Requires following the call chain from the UI zone list into the permutation code.

title: SolverException swallowed, then null parameters dereferenced
description: The Levenberg-Marquardt run is wrapped in try/catch(SolverException) that only prints the stack trace; _modelParameters stays null and the very next line constructs FourParameterLogisticSecondDrivative(null) whose value() throws NullPointerException from inside BisectionSolver, so the 'Calculate base frequency' action fails with an unrelated NPE instead of a message. Normaliser also divides by _range which is 0 when all frequencies (or all times) are identical, feeding NaN into the fit.
trigger_input: Frequency cuts that cannot be fitted by the 4PL model (e.g. two cuts, or all cuts with identical frequency so Normaliser._range==0).
suggested_fix: Rethrow as IllegalArgumentException with a user-facing message, and validate _range>0 and >=5 samples up front.
llm_value: grep-able for printStackTrace, but the downstream null path needs reading.

title: Inflection found by BisectionSolver with no root-bracketing check
description: Commons-math BisectionSolver.solve(maxEval, f, min, max, start) does not verify that f changes sign on [min,max]; if the fitted sigmoid's second derivative has no zero in the normalised time range (all cuts before or after CPA, or a monotone fit) the solver just converges to an endpoint (0.01 or 1) and returns it. inflectionTime is then the first/last cut time and inflectionFreq the curve value there - a plausible-looking but wrong F-nought that FrequencyResidualsView writes into the sensor. DopplerCurve (Apache LM variant, L158-L159) has the same issue with [0,1] where x=0 makes Math.pow(0,b-2) infinite.
trigger_input: Calculate base frequency on a frequency series that is monotonically decreasing without a CPA in the visible range.
suggested_fix: Check sign(f(min)) != sign(f(max)) (or use BracketingNthOrderBrentSolver with a bracket search) and report 'no inflection in range' instead of a value.
llm_value: Requires knowing the solver's contract and the shape of the 4PL second derivative.

title: Default TMA leg offset built with Math.toDegrees(135) where WorldVector expec...
description: setLeg() creates the fallback offset for a newly generated target leg as new WorldVector(Math.toDegrees(135), 2 NM, 0). WorldVector's bearing argument is in radians, so the value 7734.93 rad is used; modulo 2*pi this is a bearing of ~18.9 degrees (python), not the intended 135. Every auto-created leg without a preceding RelativeTMASegment (first slice of a target track) is therefore placed 2 NM at ~019 from ownship instead of 135, silently.
trigger_input: Target slicing when the secondary track has no existing RelativeTMASegment, or when the previous segment has no fixes/no matching ownship fix.
suggested_fix: Use Math.toRadians(135).
llm_value: Only detectable by knowing the WorldVector constructor's units and evaluating the expression.

title: Legs handed to the ambiguity resolver mix cuts from every visible sensor
description: resolveAmbiguousCutsB() builds each LegOfCuts with StackedDotHelper.getBearings(primary, true, period), i.e. every visible sensor's cuts in the zone (hull sonar, towed array, etc.). LegOfCuts.getCurve(CORE) then fits one quadratic through interleaved bearing series from different sensors, and the resulting slope/extrapolation used for scoring the CORE/AMBIGUOUS permutations is meaningless; the auto-slicer path (OwnshipZoneSlicer) works per-sensor so the two paths disagree.
trigger_input: Ownship with two visible sensors (e.g. hull sensor with plain bearings plus TA with ambiguous bearings) and ownship zones present; press Resolve Ambiguity.
suggested_fix: Build one LegOfCuts per (zone, sensor) and only include cuts that have an ambiguous bearing; skip legs with fewer than 3 cuts.
llm_value: Needs cross-file reasoning about what getBearings returns versus what getCurve assumes.

title: NaN base frequency written to sensor; zero step loops forever in calcSeries
description: calculateBaseFreq accepts whatever DopplerCurveFinMath returns: when the fit yields NaN (e.g. constant frequencies -> Normaliser range 0) the guard 'baseFreq != oldFreq' is true for NaN and setBaseFrequency(NaN) is persisted to the sensor, after which every predicted frequency and residual becomes NaN. calcSeries computes step=(end-start)/30 in long millis; a visible range shorter than 30 ms gives step 0 and 'for (t=start; t<=end; t+=step)' never terminates.
trigger_input: Sensor whose visible frequency cuts all read the same value (e.g. 150.00 Hz) then press 'Calculate base frequency'; or zoom the frequency plot to a <30 ms window.
suggested_fix: Reject NaN/infinite baseFreq with a message before assigning; use Math.max(1, step).
llm_value: Needs to trace NaN from Normaliser through the fit to the persisted sensor property.

title: Window eviction uses removeAll by value, desynchronising _times and _values
description: add() collects the values of out-of-window entries and calls _values.removeAll(removeValues). List.removeAll removes every element equal to any listed value, so an in-window entry whose score equals an evicted score is also removed, while its time stays in _times. From then on getAverage()/getVariance()/lastValue() are computed over the wrong set and isPopulated() (size of _times) disagrees with _values. Used by ZigDetector.runThrough on the default target-slicing path where identical scores (e.g. 0.0) are common. Python check: values [0.5,0.5,0.7] at t=0,100,200, window 150, new t=260 -> both 0.5 removed although t=100 is in-window.
trigger_input: Two fits within the window returning the same RMS score while an older entry with that score expires.
suggested_fix: Remove by index (iterate backwards and remove(i) from both lists) or store (time,value) pairs in one list.
llm_value: Requires knowing List.removeAll semantics and that scores repeat; not a pattern a grep would flag.

title: Integer division inside sqrt(numelements/(numelements-1)) makes the correctio...
description: areDeviationsInAllowedLimits (both overloads) computes Math.sqrt(numelements / (numelements - 1)) with int operands, so for n>=3 the quotient truncates to 1 and the intended factor sqrt(n/(n-1)) is never applied (python: n=3 -> 1.0 vs 1.2247, n=10 -> 1.0 vs 1.054). The Student test statistic is therefore systematically too small and outlier deviations up to ~22% (n=3) larger than the statistical limit are accepted as 'steady'. This is on the production ownship slicing path (fifo_maxdev/sieve_maxdev via AlternateLegWrapper).
trigger_input: Any steady-interval test with 3..20 fixes containing a marginal outlier heading.
suggested_fix: Cast to double: Math.sqrt((double) numelements / (numelements - 1)).
llm_value: Integer division inside a floating expression is easy to miss and its statistical effect requires reasoning.

title: walkThisEnd compares unwrapped measured bearing with 0..360 forecast without ...
description: prepareBearings() unwraps the bearing series (values such as -6 or 364 are produced, see testCleanValues), but FlanaganArctan.calcForecast() returns values in [0,360). In walkThisEnd the error is predictedB - measuredB with only a special case for measured<0 && predicted>0 && |err|>100; a measured value of 364 against a forecast of 4 gives an error of -360, flips thisAbove and inflates absError, so the grow/stop decision for the leg end is wrong near north.
trigger_input: Target bearing series crossing north, e.g. 355, 4, 2, 349 (unwrapped to 355,364,362,349) inside the leg being grown.
suggested_fix: Fold the error into [-180,180) (as FlanaganArctan.function already does) before using it, and drop the ad-hoc measured<0 test.
llm_value: Needs to connect the unwrapped domain produced in one method with the [0,360) domain produced in another.

title: runThrough re-runs Nelder-Mead over the growing window per cut and prints eve...
description: For every cut index 'end' runThrough calls optimiseThis() (Nelder-Mead, Nmax=116400) over subList(start,end), and FlanaganArctan.function is O(window) per evaluation, so the default target slicer (sliceTarget -> sliceThis, chosen because USE_HOLISTIC_SLICER has no default) is O(n^2 * iterations) per ownship leg and is run forward and backward. It also System.out.println's every forecast for every fit (L2110-L2120) and logs 'scores:' lines, and growLeg/runThrough2 log to the Eclipse error log on each step. This runs on the UI thread from the slice action.
trigger_input: Ownship leg containing ~1000 sensor cuts; press the target 'slice' button.
suggested_fix: Remove the per-cut println/log calls, cap the fit window (the commented-out 'end-20' line), and run slicing in a Job with progress.
llm_value: Complexity is only evident from the nested optimiser call inside the per-cut loop.

title: Ambiguous BRT bearing course-relBearing is never wrapped into 0-360 (negative...
description: loadThese computes bearingDegs = course + relBearing and subtracts 360 once if >= 360, and ambigDegs = course - relBearing with the same >= 360 check only (L408-L418). Whenever the relative bearing exceeds the ownship course (e.g. course 010, rel 069) the ambiguous bearing is -59 and is stored as such in SensorContactWrapper; large relative bearings (>350 with a high course) can also leave values >= 720. Cuts outside the track's time span are silently skipped (L404) with no count reported.
trigger_input: BRT file '1263297600.000000, 69.00' against a towed-array track whose course at that time is 010 deg
suggested_fix: Normalise both bearings with ((x % 360) + 360) % 360 and report the number of skipped cuts.
llm_value: Sign case is only apparent from the arithmetic; grep for '-= 360' would not reveal the missing negative branch.

title: STRAND flat-file export uses default-locale DecimalFormat, emitting comma dec...
description: collateLine and getBody2 create DecimalFormat('0.00'), ('0.0'), ('0'), ('0.####') and ('0.########') without locale symbols (L437-L439; L712-L713). On a JVM whose default locale uses a comma decimal separator (verified: Locale.GERMANY formats 1234.5 as '1234,50') the tab-separated numeric columns contain commas and the external consumer of the STRAND scenario report misreads or rejects the file. Msd_Depth (L925) is additionally written with Double.toString, giving a mixed style.
trigger_input: Run the flat-file (STRAND) export on a workstation with a German/French/Spanish locale
suggested_fix: Build every DecimalFormat with DecimalFormatSymbols(Locale.UK) (or Locale.ROOT) and format Msd_Depth the same way.
llm_value: grep-able

title: OTH-GOLD month names parsed with default-locale GMTDateFormat; every POS date...
description: dateFor parses the month token with GMTDateFormat('MMMyy') and 'ddHHmm'Z'MMMyy' (L482-L484; L496-L497); GMTDateFormat(String) calls SimpleDateFormat(pattern) with the default locale (GMTDateFormat.java L41). Verified: with a German default locale 'AUG'/'OCT'/'MAR' tokens throw ParseException. dateFor logs and returns null, and produceFix (see the null-deref row) still creates a FixWrapper with a null time, so on a non-English JVM every OTH position is undated and the import subsequently fails.
trigger_input: OTH-GOLD file with 'POS/112313Z1/AUG/4612N34/02122W7//...' lines imported on a French-locale JVM
suggested_fix: Use the GMTDateFormat(pattern, Locale.ENGLISH) constructor (note: that overload currently forgets setLenient(false)).
llm_value: Requires following GMTDateFormat to see which constructor applies the default locale.

title: produceFix never returns null and POS-before-CTC dereferences a null track, c...
description: produceFix (L674-L682) wraps whatever locationFrom/dateFor returned, even null location or date, so the 'wrapped != null' guard at L738 is always true; a POS line with a bad date leads to thisDate==null and thisDate.getDate() at L747 (or TrackWrapper.addFix with a null DTG) throwing NullPointerException. A POS line that precedes any CTC line dereferences thisTrack==null at L733. readOTHData declares only IOException, so these RuntimeExceptions abort the import instead of being logged like the other field errors.
trigger_input: OTH file whose first data line is 'POS/...' with no preceding 'CTC/...' line, or a POS line with month 'ABC'
suggested_fix: Return null from produceFix when loc or date is null (and log), and skip POS lines while thisTrack is null with an ErrorLogger message.
llm_value: Needs to see that the null guard is vacuous because the callee cannot return null.

title: Corrupt $POSL sentence crashes NMEA import (NPE on first OS_POS, SIOOBE in de...
description: In the OS_POS branch parseOwnship may return null (typePattern is looser than osPattern), but state.location is dereferenced at L837 before the null check at L841 whenever origin is still null, so a truncated or malformed first position sentence throws NullPointerException. degsFor (L453-457) assumes a '.' is present; the lat/long regex groups use an unescaped '.' so '3409x5794,N' passes the regex and text.substring(0, dec-2) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException (verified). Neither is caught (only IOException at L881), so the whole import fails.
trigger_input: NMEA log whose first '$POSL,POS,GPS,...' line is truncated after the source field, or contains '3409x5794,N' in the latitude field
suggested_fix: Check state for null before using it; escape the decimal point in the regexes (\\.) and validate indexOf('.') >= 2 in degsFor, skipping the sentence with a logged warning.
llm_value: Needs ordering analysis of the null check vs use and regex-vs-substring assumptions.

title: Ownship speed computed from consecutive fixes with identical timestamps gives...
description: Position sentences carry no time; the date comes from the last $POSL,DZA line. With osFreq=0 storeLocation accepts a fix whenever date >= lastTime+0, so several POS/POS2 sentences between two DZA lines get the same Date. fixFor then divides travelled distance by timeDiffMillis==0 (L486-487), storing speed Infinity (or NaN when distance is also 0) in the FixWrapper; course from a zero-length vector is also arbitrary. These values propagate into the track and any analysis using speed.
trigger_input: Log where the GPS emits two '$POSL,POS,GPS,...' sentences between consecutive '$POSL,DZA,...' timestamps, imported with ownship frequency 0
suggested_fix: When timeDiffMillis == 0 reuse the previous fix's course/speed (or skip the duplicate-time fix).
llm_value: Needs to combine the DZA-driven timestamp model with the resampling predicate to see equal timestamps are reachable.

title: Argos x/y to bearing uses atan2(y, x) while sibling PMRF importer uses atan2(...
description: ImportArgosFix converts range-data x/y offsets to a WorldVector with brg = Math.atan2(y, x) (L175), i.e. a mathematical angle from the x axis, whereas ImportPMRFFix (L222, annotated 'IM experimenting') uses Math.atan2(x, y), the compass bearing from north expected by WorldVector. For east/north offsets one of the two mirrors every position about the NE diagonal (bearing b becomes 90-b). Since both feed WorldVector(brg, range, depth) and WorldLocation.add, the two importers cannot both be right.
trigger_input: Argos .rao line with x=1000, y=0 (due east of origin) is plotted due north
suggested_fix: Confirm the coordinate convention of the .rao format and use atan2(x, y) for east/north offsets in both importers; add a unit test with a known offset.
llm_value: Requires comparing two sibling importers and knowing WorldVector's bearing convention.

title: ;BRG: importer reads five latitude tokens and exporter writes an incompatible...
description: readThisLine reads latDeg, latMin, latSec and then reads latMin and latSec again (L206-L211), consuming five tokens for the latitude, so for a well-formed 'D M S H' latitude the hemisphere letter is fed to readThisDouble, ParseException is caught and null returned (the line is silently dropped). exportThis (L141-L158) writes 'BD start end' with no date/time and no orientation/length, which readThisLine cannot parse either, so bearing lines never round-trip. No sample data or docs in the repository contain ';BRG:', suggesting the path is untested.
trigger_input: ';BRG: @A 951212 050200 22 10 53.54 N 21 45 14.20 W 45.0 5000 my bearing' is silently ignored
suggested_fix: Delete the duplicated latMin/latSec reads and make exportThis emit symbology, DTG, start location, orientation and length.
llm_value: Duplicate-statement bug only visible by reading the token sequence against the format.

title: Exporting an untimed ellipse stamps it with the current wall-clock time
description: exportThis substitutes new HiResDate(new Date()) when the shape has no start DTG (L201-L207) and writes it into the ;ELLIPSE: line. On re-import the ellipse acquires a start time equal to the export moment, so a permanently visible ellipse becomes time-filtered and disappears from plots of the original data period. The exported colour is also hard-coded 'BD' (colour lost), as in ImportCircle/ImportRectangle/ImportWheel exporters.
trigger_input: Export a REP containing an ellipse created without a time, then import it into a 1995 dataset
suggested_fix: Write a NULL/absent date token that readThisLine accepts (as ImportSensorArc does), or refuse to fake a date; export the real colour via replaySymbolFor.
llm_value: Needs the reader side to see that an invented date changes visibility semantics.

title: ;LINE: end point uses Integer.parseInt while start point accepts decimals; de...
description: extractStart parses the first location with MWCXMLReader.readThisDouble (decimal degrees/minutes allowed, L102-L121), but the end location parses degrees and minutes with Integer.parseInt (L216-L217, L229-L235). A line such as ';LINE: @B 20.5 0 0 N 21 10 0 W 22.5 0 0 N 21 10 0 W x' throws NumberFormatException, which escapes readThisLine and aborts the whole REP import at that line ('Number format error'), while the same value in the start position is accepted.
suggested_fix: Use readThisDouble for the end-point degrees and minutes (or share extractStart for both ends).
llm_value: Inconsistency between two halves of one parser; grep for parseInt would give many false positives.

title: Planning legs exported with default-locale DecimalFormat; comma decimals are ...
description: exportThis formats depth, range, duration, speed and course with new DecimalFormat('0.######') using the platform default locale (L206; L223; L269-L273; L296). Verified: with Locale.GERMANY 12.5 formats as '12,5'. The importers read these fields with MWCXMLReader.readThisDouble, which (see the MWCXMLReader row) parses '12,5' as 12.0, so on a non-English workstation a planning track survives export/import with truncated ranges, speeds and courses and no error.
trigger_input: Export a planning track with leg speed 12.5 kts on a German-locale JVM and re-import it
suggested_fix: Construct the DecimalFormat with DecimalFormatSymbols(Locale.UK) as DebriefFormatLocation does.
llm_value: grep-able (new DecimalFormat without symbols), but the silent-truncation consequence depends on the reader.

title: Unchecked casts and substring(6) on user-controlled names throw uncaught runt...
description: Track names from the file are used to look up layers and cast without instanceof: L1916 (TrackWrapper) getLayerFor(theTrack) throws ClassCastException when a fix's track name equals an existing non-track layer such as 'Annotations' or 'Narratives'; L2127 does the same for ;SENSOR: lines and L2228 casts to DynamicShapeLayer for dynamic shapes. processContactWrapper (L1710) and processDynamicShapeWrapper (L1783) call trackName.substring(6) on unknown track names shorter than 6 characters, throwing StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. canImportThisFile (L1314-1315) throws on a name without '.'. importRep only catches NumberFormat/IO/NoSuchElement/Parse exceptions (L1618-L1630), so these propagate and the import fails without a readError dialog.
trigger_input: REP file with a ';TEXT:' line (creates layer 'Annotations') followed by a fix line whose track is named Annotations; or ';TMA_POS: 030211 120312 CAR S@ ...' where no track 'CAR' exists
suggested_fix: Guard with instanceof and length checks, report via readError, and add a catch(RuntimeException) in importRep that routes to handleException.
llm_value: Requires tracing which layer types can share the Layers namespace and the exception filter in importRep.

title: Exported ;TIMETEXT: line omits the date/time and colour, so it cannot be re-i...
description: exportThis writes ';TIMETEXT: BB <location><label>' (hard-coded symbology, no DTG, no space before the label) whereas readThisLine expects symbology, date, time, then location (L165-L169). Re-importing an exported file makes DebriefFormatDateTime.parseThis receive the latitude degrees as the date and throws ParseException, which aborts the whole REP import with a 'Date format error'. suggested_fix: Dispose GC/Image in a finally block around the paint; catch NumberFormatException and fall back to 255.

No SHA-256 is checked although AdoptOpenJDK publishes one. Integrity rests entirely on TLS to github.com and on the (archived) AdoptOpenJDK org's release assets never being replaced; the result is cached for the lifetime of key `win-jre-11.0.5-10` (L150) so a single poisoned download persists across every build.

suggested_fix: Download the matching .sha256.txt and run `sha256sum -c` before unzip; include the hash in the cache key.

title: Third-party actions referenced by mutable tags; xvfb-action wraps the whole b...
description: Every `uses:` is a floating major tag rather than a commit SHA: GabrielBB/xvfb-action@v1 (L176) runs the entire `mvn clean verify` and is an archived, unmaintained repository; softprops/action-gh-release@v2 (L311) receives the contents:write GITHUB_TOKEN and decides what is published; andstor/file-existence-action@v1 (L218) and bcomnes/cleanup-xvfb@v1 (L327) are small personal actions. A moved tag (as in the tj-actions/changed-files incident, CVE-2025-30066) executes attacker code inside the release job.

suggested_fix: Pin every action to a full commit SHA with a version comment and enable Dependabot `github-actions` updates; replace xvfb-action with `xvfb-run -a mvn ...` (xvfb is already apt-installed at L117) so no third-party action wraps the build.

title: contents:write granted to the build job on every event, not just tag releases
description: L88-89 `permissions: contents: write` applies to the whole `buildandrelease` job for push, pull_request and workflow_dispatch alike, yet only the `Upload release` step (L310-324) needs it. On a same-repository branch PR or a workflow_dispatch of any branch, the untrusted-ish `mvn clean verify` (L174-179, which executes every module's antrun/pom logic) runs with a token able to push branches, move tags and create releases. Combined with `on.push.tags: '*'` (L15-16), any actor able to push a `YYYYMMDD_N_N_N` tag publishes a public release with RELEASE_NOTES.md as body (L303-316); the file relies on repository tag-protection rules that cannot be seen from the repo.
trigger_input: workflow_dispatch on a feature branch whose pom adds an antrun `<exec>` that uses $ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN to `git push origin HEAD:develop` or create a release.
suggested_fix: Keep the job at `contents: read`, move the release upload into a separate `release` job with `needs: build`, `if: startsWith(github.ref,'refs/tags/')` and its own `permissions: contents: write`, consuming the product zips via upload/download-artifact; add a tag protection ruleset for `????????_*`.
llm_value: Needs reasoning about which steps actually consume the permission and about the event matrix; a linter only flags missing permissions blocks.

title: Release can publish with assets silently missing (MSI check is non-blocking)
description: softprops/action-gh-release@v2 (L311-324) is used with its default `fail_on_unmatched_files: false`, so any of the seven listed paths that does not exist is skipped without error. The MSI check (L216-221) sets `allow_failure: true`, and `org.mwc.debrief.legacy/dist/DebriefLegacy*.jar` / `org.mwc.debrief.lite/dist/debrief-lite*.zip` (L322-323) are globs whose directories are only created by module-level ant targets. RELEASING.md L87-89 and SKILL.md step 9 promise seven assets, but the workflow only guarantees the ones that happen to exist. Because `build installer` (L196-215) has no `if: always()`, a failed msitools build instead aborts the job before upload, so the intended 'MSI optional' behaviour is inconsistent either way.
trigger_input: ftp.gnome.org redirect changes or wixl-heat errors: the run stays green (or MSI step fails) and the GitHub release has 6 (or 0) assets.
suggested_fix: Set `fail_on_unmatched_files: true`, drop `allow_failure`, and make the installer step fail loudly; verify asset count in the release job.
llm_value: Needs knowledge of action-gh-release's default and cross-reading RELEASING.md to see the promised invariant.

The file is dead (last touched 2021-09-29, travis-ci.org is shut down, GitHub Actions replaced it) and also still describes a Windows32Bit artifact (L71) that no longer exists, so it misleads about the release process.

title: Feature mapping misses non-org.mwc plugins shipped in the features
description: FEATURE_FOR_PREFIX (L56-60) only maps org.mwc.asset/cmap/debrief prefixes, but org.mwc.cmap.combined.feature/feature.xml ships org.eclipse.nebula.cwt, org.eclipse.nebula.widgets.cdatetime and org.eclipse.nebula.jface.cdatetime, and org.mwc.debrief.combined.feature ships org.freehep. features_for() (L333-339) therefore does not bump the feature when only those bundles changed, which violates the invariant stated at L362-365 ('If a plugin moves, the feature that ships it has to move too or the P2 update site will never offer the new bundle'). The always-bumped org.mwc.debrief.core masks this for the debrief feature but not for the cmap feature. Separately, org.mwc.asset.core.feature is mapped (L57) although root pom.xml L48-50 excludes it from the build.
trigger_input: Release where the only cmap-side change is in org.eclipse.nebula.cwt: cmap.combined.feature keeps its version, P2 clients never receive the fixed bundle.
suggested_fix: Derive the mapping by parsing each feature.xml's <plugin id=...> list instead of prefixes, and warn when a bumped plugin is in no built feature.
llm_value: Required cross-checking the prefix table against the actual feature.xml contents and the root pom module list.

title: Target platform resolves Eclipse p2 repositories over plain http
description: Three of the repository locations Tycho resolves on every CI build are cleartext: L42 http://download.eclipse.org/releases/2021-03, L45 http://download.eclipse.org/releases/2021-12, L95 http://download.eclipse.org/nebula/releases/2.5.0/ (and eclipse-latest.tpd L6, L46, L52 mirror this). p2 checks artifact checksums only against artifacts.xml fetched over the same channel, so an on-path attacker who intercepts before the server's https redirect can substitute bundles that end up in the shipped product and in the develop-written ~/.p2 cache (main.yml L181-189) restored by every later build including tag releases.

trigger_input: MITM of CI egress during target resolution on a develop push; poisoned bundle persists via the m2-tycho cache.
suggested_fix: Change the six locations to https:// (the other repositories in the same file already are) and regenerate the .target from the .tpd.

suggested_fix: Wrap each parse, log and skip the property.

PlotTracks assigns marker/animation ids, z-order and (via get(0)) the time captions from that order, so two exports of the same plot with renamed tracks render differently and the caption source track is arbitrary.
trigger_input: Export the same scenario twice after renaming one track.

title: GDAL executables copied to and run from the shared temp root; predictable wor...
description: On Windows, prepareGdalEnvironment() copies gdalwarp.exe/gdal_create.exe and their DLLs directly under java.io.tmpdir (L282) and executes them from there (L434, L574); PROJ_LIB is also pointed at tmpdir. All GeoJSON/composition work files go to tmpdir/<millis> (L156, L513-L520). Anything else able to write to the user's temp folder can plant a DLL/exe that Debrief then executes (DLL search order includes the exe's directory). REPLACE_EXISTING mitigates the exe itself but not extra DLLs. || getFile/createTempFile build paths as <java.io.tmpdir>/<millis timestamp>/<layerName>.geojson and open them with PrintWriter (L491-L521) without O_EXCL/createTempFile, so on a multi-user Unix /tmp a local attacker who pre-creates the directory or a symlink can redirect the write or feed a substituted GeoJSON/composition XML to gdal. On Windows createTemporaryEnvironmentWindows copies the gdal executables and PROJ data into <tmpdir>/windows/... (L100-L130, L282-L285) and then executes them (L574), so a writable temp dir becomes the trusted binary location (REPLACE_EXISTING mitigates pre-planting of listed files but not extra DLLs loaded by gdal). Layer names from the data file feed into file names via sanitizeFilename (L534) which strips path separators, so traversal is prevented.
trigger_input: Attacker-controlled DLL named as one of the GDAL dependencies present in %TEMP% before the first GeoPDF export.
suggested_fix: Extract into a freshly created, uniquely named directory (Files.createTempDirectory) with restrictive permissions, or ship the binaries inside the plugin install and run them in place.
llm_value: Needed to combine the copy destination, the exec call and DLL search-order behaviour.

suggested_fix: try-with-resources for PDDocument; log through logThisError and propagate a failure status.

title: Temp unpack directory left behind on failed export or dimension lookup
description: checkPathandInitialization() creates a temp dir (L153); it is removed only by PackPresentation.pack() on the success path (L515) or at the end of retrieveMapProperties() (L758). Any exception in createPptxFromTrackData() or FindMap.getMapDetails() leaves a full unpacked copy of the template in java.io.tmpdir; validateDonorFile does clean up (L836-L842) but the other two entry points do not.
trigger_input: Export against a template that fails at getShapes() or writeSoup(); repeat several times and observe Debrief_to_pptx_* folders accumulating.
suggested_fix: Wrap the body in try/finally that deletes temp_unpack_path unless pack() consumed it.
llm_value: grep-able

title: ParseException from track timestamps printed and ignored, partial data returned
description: parse() catches ParseException from parseTracks() with printStackTrace and returns a TrackData holding whatever tracks were parsed before the bad point; the PlotGpx CLI then exports a truncated presentation without any error. Also lat/lon are parsed into float (L427-L428), losing precision below ~1e-5 deg.
trigger_input: GPX-like track file whose second <trkpt><time> is malformed.
suggested_fix: Propagate the exception (or a DebriefException) to the caller; use double for coordinates.
llm_value: grep-able

title: Default unpack path deletes any existing sibling directory of the template
description: With the one-arg overload the unpack folder is pptx_path minus its last 5 characters (assumes '.pptx'), then L55-L57 mkdir it and L59-L65 unconditionally FileUtils.deleteDirectory() it. Any pre-existing directory that shares the template's base name (e.g. 'Brief/' beside 'Brief.pptx') is recursively deleted. Only the unit test uses this overload today, but the API is public.
trigger_input: Call unpackFunction('/data/Brief.pptx') when /data/Brief/ already exists and holds user files.
suggested_fix: Never delete a directory the caller did not create: fail if it exists, or always unpack into Files.createTempDirectory() as PlotTracks does; strip the extension with lastIndexOf('.').
llm_value: Needed to reason about the mkdir-then-delete sequence rather than a pattern match.

title: Directory-history .cfg in user.home deserialized without filter
description: The constructor builds <user.home>/<app>_DIRECTORY_HISTORY.cfg (L550-L551) and, if it exists, reads it with a plain ObjectInputStream.readObject() cast to Vector<String> (L554-L556). Static fields fis/ois/comboModel/dirFile (L445-L448) are shared across instances. Exploitation needs write access to the user's home directory, so impact is low, but it is another unfiltered deserialization sink in the Swing tooling.

suggested_fix: Store the history as plain text (one path per line) or java.util.Properties; if serialization is kept add an ObjectInputFilter allowing only Vector and String.
llm_value: grep-able

title: DPF-supplied absolute SourceFile path opened from the local filesystem
description: elementClosed takes the SourceFile attribute from the .dpf/.xml being imported, checks only that new File(_sourceFile).exists() (L93-L96) and hands it to the S57 layer, which then reads that file through S57 BinaryFile/URLInputReader (BinaryFile L142-L151 also accepts http: URLs and opens them with URL.openStream). A data file can therefore make Debrief read any local path or fetch a remote URL when the layer is painted; the contents are parsed as S57 so no direct disclosure, but it is an untrusted-path sink and an outbound network trigger.
trigger_input: .dpf containing <s57 SourceFile="http://attacker.example/beacon"/> or SourceFile="/etc/passwd".
suggested_fix: Resolve SourceFile relative to the plot file's directory, reject absolute paths and URLs unless the user confirms, and restrict to *.000 S57 cells.
llm_value: Requires following the attribute from the XML handler into the S57 loader's URL handling.

title: Memento strings deserialized with permissive XStream.fromXML
description: restorePreviousPlot creates `new XStream(new DomDriver())` (L1112) with no allowTypes/denyTypes and calls fromXML on eight memento strings (L1119, L1128, L1150-L1174), casting afterwards. With the bundled 1.4.12 (see supply-chain row) an attacker who can edit the workspace's .metadata/.plugins/org.eclipse.ui.workbench/workbench.xml (or a shared/imported workspace) gets arbitrary object construction at workbench start-up. Casting a non-String result also throws ClassCastException outside the try so the view fails to restore.
trigger_input: workbench.xml with <view id=org.mwc.cmap.xyplot.views.XYPlotView> whose DATA attribute holds an XStream gadget payload (e.g. the CVE-2021-29505 chain).
suggested_fix: Call xs.allowTypeHierarchy(AbstractSeriesDataset.class), xs.allowTypes for formattingOperation, String, Integer, Boolean and deny everything else; store scalar attributes as plain memento strings.
llm_value: Needs knowledge of the XStream security model and where memento data lives.

title: setScaleVal/offsetOrigin NPE on null data area; negative zoom clamps
description: offsetOrigin() checks getScreenArea() for null but not getDataArea(), then calls getDataArea().getWidth() and getDataArea().getCentre(); setScaleVal() (exposed as the 'Scaling factor' property in FlatProjectionInfo) calls offsetOrigin(true) unconditionally, so editing the property before any data is loaded throws NPE. zoom(value) with a negative factor makes _scaleVal negative, which offsetOrigin clamps to 2e-7 (maximum zoom-in) instead of rejecting it.
trigger_input: Open the projection properties on an empty plot and edit Scaling factor; or a zoom action computed with a negative factor.
suggested_fix: Guard getDataArea()==null in offsetOrigin and reject non-positive zoom factors.

title: toWorld mirrors longitude about the centre; zoom() is a no-op
description: getPoint(double,double) maps x to (x - centerMap)*latScale*scale + centerScreen, but the inverse getPoint(int,int) returns centerMap - (xs - centerScreen)/(latScale*scale), i.e. 2*centerMap - x (python check: x=13, centre 10 -> 7). The inverse also evaluates latScale at a different latitude than the forward transform, and zoom() is empty so the projection cannot be zoomed. Also uses PI=3.1415927 and '|' instead of '||' at L58. Class is unreferenced (dead).
trigger_input: Enable JMapTransformMercator: clicking on the plot reports a longitude reflected about the screen centre.
suggested_fix: Remove the class, or fix the sign in the inverse and implement zoom.
llm_value: Sign error visible only by algebraically inverting the forward transform.

title: Integer division zeroes ellipsoid terms; sin(lat^3); (long) cast precedence
description: setEllipse computes _A0 = 1 - 1/4*_e2 - 3/64*_e4 - 5/256*_e6 etc. with integer literals, so 1/4, 3/64, 3/8, 15/256, 35/3072 evaluate to 0 and _A0=1, _A2=_A4=_A6=0 (python: correct A0=0.99832, A2=0.00252). mParts uses 1/3*_e4 and 1/5*_e6 (=0) and Math.sin(Math.pow(lat,3)) instead of sin(lat)^3 (error 0.033 arc-min at 60N). In toWorld, ((long) mParts(lat2) * 10000) casts before multiplying, so the bisection compares whole arc-minutes and stops with up to 1 arc-minute error. The class is currently only referenced in a commented-out line of AWTChart, so impact is latent. Mercator3 repeats the same expressions (L158-L159, L215-L220).
trigger_input: Enable Mercator2 as the chart projection: latitude round trips are quantised to ~1 nm and the ellipsoidal corrections are dropped.
suggested_fix: Use double literals (1.0/4, 3.0/64 ...), Math.pow(Math.sin(lat),3), and (long)(mParts(lat2)*10000) or a direct double comparison.
llm_value: Integer-literal division inside double expressions is a classic reading-level bug; CodeQL has a rule for it but the cast-precedence and sin(lat^3) errors need the formula.

title: toScreen swaps latitude and longitude; central meridian set from a latitude
description: toScreen assigns d1 = getLong() and d2 = getLat(), then wraps d2 (latitude) by +/-360 relative to _centralMeridian and feeds d1 (longitude) into tan(45 + 0.5*d1) as if it were latitude; rescale() sets _centralMeridian = wa.getBottomRight().getLat(). Output ignores the screen size and _scaleVal entirely (returns metres in nautical-mile units), and toWorld is the inverse of a different formula, so toScreen/toWorld do not round-trip. Class is unreferenced (dead) apart from itself.
trigger_input: Instantiate Mercator3 as the chart projection: every location is plotted with lat/long transposed and off-screen.
suggested_fix: Delete the class or rewrite toScreen using lat for the tan term and long for the meridian offset with the screen scale applied.
llm_value: Variable names d1..d9 hide the transposition; only reading the trig identifies which argument is which.

title: Constructor truncates to whole milliseconds despite microsecond units
description: The constructor stores (long) convert(units, MILLISECONDS, value), so any sub-millisecond duration is truncated (verified: new Duration(0.5, MILLISECONDS).getMillis()==0 and new Duration(500, MICROSECONDS).getMillis()==0) even though a MICROSECONDS unit is offered and the field comment says microseconds. round() also uses an asymmetric 0.51 threshold and floors negatives.
trigger_input: Time-step or trail-length of 0.5 ms configured in a .dpf Stepper element is silently loaded as 0.
suggested_fix: Store microseconds (or a double) internally and round rather than truncate when converting.
llm_value: grep-able

title: intersects() returns inverted period for disjoint inputs
description: intersects() takes max(start) and min(end) without checking they are ordered, so two non-overlapping periods yield a period whose start is after its end (verified: [0,10] intersect [20,30] -> start 20000us, end 10000us, isConsistent=false) with no null/empty signal; BearingResidualsView uses the result to bound plots. isConsistent() uses strict < although its javadoc says 'before or equals', so a zero-length period is inconsistent.
trigger_input: Sensor data coverage entirely outside the visible period in the bearing residuals view: inverted plot range.
suggested_fix: Return null (or an empty marker) when startP > endP and document it; use <= in isConsistent.
llm_value: grep-able

title: setCentredWidth/Height no-ops (WorldVector arg order); getCentre aliasing
description: setCentredWidth builds new WorldVector(newWidth - getWidth(), 0, 0), but the constructor signature is (bearingRads, rangeDegs, depth), so the width delta is used as a bearing with zero range and extend() does nothing; verified an area of width 2 stays width 2 after setCentredWidth(4). In addition getCentre() returns the single mutable _thisCentre instance, so originalCenter (held by these methods) is overwritten by setCentre's own getCentre() call, and external holders such as FlatProjection._dataOrigin alias the area's internal centre.
trigger_input: Any future caller of setCentredWidth (currently unused) gets an unchanged area; code storing getCentre() then mutating the area sees its stored value change.
suggested_fix: Pass the delta as the range (bearing pi/2), return a copy from getCentre(), or remove the unused methods.
llm_value: grep-able

title: equals compares converted doubles exactly while hashCode uses raw value+units
description: equals() returns getValueIn(DEGS) == other.getValueIn(DEGS) (exact floating comparison of two converted values) whereas hashCode() hashes _myDistance and _myUnits, so objects the class deems equal hash differently. Verified by compiling: new WorldDistance(60, MINUTES).equals(new WorldDistance(1, DEGS)) is true (the inline test asserts this) but their hashCodes differ. Conversions that are not bit-exact (e.g. yards vs kyds) can also make equal physical distances unequal.
trigger_input: WorldDistance values stored in a HashSet (e.g. distinct range-ring radii) with the same length in different units.
suggested_fix: Hash the canonical value (e.g. Double.hashCode of getValueIn(METRES)) and compare with a small relative tolerance or Double.compare on the canonical unit.
llm_value: grep-able

title: Tolerance-based equals() without hashCode(); non-transitive equality
description: equals(WorldLocation) accepts lat/long within 1e-11 deg but requires exact depth equality, and the class does not override hashCode(), so equal locations have different identity hash codes (verified: two identical WorldLocation(1,2,3) report equals=true, hashCode equal=false), breaking HashMap/HashSet semantics; tolerance equality is also non-transitive. equals(WorldLocation) also dereferences a null argument.
trigger_input: WorldLocation used as a HashSet element or HashMap key (e.g. de-duplicating fixes): duplicates are not detected.
suggested_fix: Either compare exactly (Double.compare) and add a matching hashCode, or drop equals override in favour of an explicit approxEquals method.

title: Emits 60.00 seconds and 60 minutes fields in Debrief/REP location text
description: brokenDown truncates minutes with (int) and only zeroes seconds when sec > 59.99999, so seconds in (59.995, 59.99999] are formatted by the 00.00 pattern as 60.00; when the carry does fire, min++ can reach 60 with no carry into degrees. Verified by compiling: WorldLocation(12.34999..., 12.99999999) formats as "12 20 60.00 N 012 59 60.00 E". The numeric value round-trips on re-import (12+59/60+60/3600 = 13.0) but the text violates the DDD MM SS.SS format contract and breaks any consumer validating 0<=SS<60.
trigger_input: Export a fix at latitude 12.9999999 to .rep.
suggested_fix: Round to the output resolution first (e.g. work in hundredths of a second as a long) and carry seconds->minutes->degrees.
